description: 1. Lay a colorful mat on a flat floor. 2. Place the child on their belly. 3. Put a mirror or high-contrast toy in front of them to encourage neck lifting.
activity_photo: [Image: Baby lifting head on tummy]

description: 1. Lay the child on their back. 2. Shake a rattle to one side of their head. 3. Move the rattle slowly toward the floor to guide their body to roll over to reach it.
activity_photo: [Image: Infant reaching while rolling]

description: 1. Sit the child on a firm surface. 2. Place supportive pillows around their back and sides. 3. Place a toy in front of them to encourage staying upright.
activity_photo: [Image: Baby sitting with pillows]

description: 1. Get into a crawling position with the child. 2. Roll a ball just out of their reach. 3. Cheer as they move forward to "catch" the ball.
activity_photo: [Image: Child crawling toward ball]

description: 1. Place a toy at the far end of a sturdy sofa. 2. Help the child stand and hold the furniture. 3. Encourage side-steps toward the toy.
activity_photo: [Image: Child walking along sofa]

description: 1. Position the child behind a stable walker. 2. Assist their grip on the handle. 3. Encourage them to push it forward toward you.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pushing a walker]

description: 1. Place a soft ball in front of the child's feet. 2. Demonstrate a kicking motion. 3. Hold their hand for balance as they try to swing their leg at the ball.
activity_photo: [Image: Child swinging leg at ball]

description: 1. Place a strip of colored tape on the floor. 2. Hold the child's hands. 3. Guide them to walk one foot in front of the other along the line.
activity_photo: [Image: Child walking on tape line]

description: 1. Stack several firm sofa cushions on a carpeted floor. 2. Place a toy on top of the stack. 3. Help the child crawl up the cushions to retrieve it.
activity_photo: [Image: Child climbing over pillows]

description: 1. Stand on a flat, soft surface. 2. Hold the child’s hands for support. 3. Count "1, 2, 3, Jump!" and encourage them to bend their knees and hop off the floor.
activity_photo: [Image: Child hopping with parent]

description: 1. Place a toy two steps up on a staircase. 2. Support the child at the hips. 3. Encourage them to reach for the next step and pull their knees up.
activity_photo: [Image: Child crawling up steps]

description: 1. Set up a play tunnel or a row of open boxes. 2. Sit at the far end and call the child’s name. 3. Encourage them to crawl through the dark space to find you.
activity_photo: [Image: Child peering through tunnel]

description: 1. Play upbeat music with a clear rhythm. 2. Hold the child's hands and bounce or sway. 3. Encourage them to spin, clap, or wiggle their hips to the beat.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent and child dancing]

description: 1. Stand a short distance from the child. 2. Demonstrate an overhand or underhand throw with a soft ball. 3. Encourage them to throw the ball toward a target like a basket.
activity_photo: [Image: Child throwing ball into bin]

description: 1. Arrange pillows and toys in a path. 2. Guide the child by the hand through the path. 3. Encourage them to step over the pillows and weave through the toys.
activity_photo: [Image: Child stepping over a pillow]

description: 1. Call out an animal (e.g., "Bear"). 2. Show the child how to crawl on hands and feet like a bear. 3. Change to a "Frog" and show them how to squat and hop.
activity_photo: [Image: Child hopping like a frog]

description: 1. Place your hands on top of your head like ears. 2. Demonstrate short, quick hops. 3. Encourage the child to follow you around the room hopping on both feet.
activity_photo: [Image: Child jumping with hands on head]

description: 1. Play a rhythmic "marching" song. 2. Encourage the child to lift their knees high with each step. 3. Swing your arms in sync with your legs to show the motion.
activity_photo: [Image: Child marching in a line]

description: 1. Stand a few feet away from the child. 2. Gently roll a ball toward their feet. 3. Encourage them to wait for the ball and kick it back to you as it arrives.
activity_photo: [Image: Child kicking a moving ball]

description: 1. Walk around the room performing an action (e.g., clapping). 2. Tell the child to "Do what I do!". 3. Change the action to something else, like touching your nose or hopping.
activity_photo: [Image: Child walking behind parent]

description: 1. Place 4-5 firm pillows in a straight or curved line on a carpeted floor. 2. Hold the child's hands as they step from one pillow to the next. 3. Encourage them to maintain balance on the uneven surface until they reach the end.
activity_photo: [Image: Child stepping on a pillow path]

description: 1. Stand at one end of a clear room. 2. Tell the child to run toward you when you say "Go!". 3. Shout "Stop!" and show them how to freeze in place, then repeat the cycle.
activity_photo: [Image: Child freezing in a running pose]

description: 1. Place a weighted laundry basket or a large toy box on a smooth floor. 2. Show the child how to place both hands on the side. 3. Encourage them to use their legs to push the object across the room to a "finish line."
activity_photo: [Image: Child pushing a heavy box]

description: 1. Place several low objects (like pool noodles or rolled towels) on the floor. 2. Lead the child toward the obstacles. 3. Encourage them to lift one leg high to step over without touching the object.
activity_photo: [Image: Child lifting leg over a towel]

description: 1. Gently toss a bright balloon into the air. 2. Encourage the child to look up and follow its movement. 3. Have them run or reach out to tap the balloon to keep it from hitting the ground.
activity_photo: [Image: Child reaching for a floating balloon]

description: 1. Blow several bubbles toward the floor. 2. Point to the bubbles as they land. 3. Encourage the child to run and "stomp" on the bubbles with their feet to pop them.
activity_photo: [Image: Child's foot popping a bubble]

description: 1. Set up "hurdles" using small blocks with a stick across them. 2. Hold the child's hand for support. 3. Guide them to step over each hurdle carefully, focusing on lifting their knees.
tools: Toy blocks and a wooden dowel
activity_photo: [Image: Child stepping over a small hurdle]

description: 1. Tell the child you are "sneaking" like a quiet mouse. 2. Demonstrate walking on the balls of your feet with heels lifted. 3. Encourage them to follow you quietly across the room on their tiptoes.
activity_photo: [Image: Child walking on tiptoes]

description: 1. Stand facing the child and hold their hands. 2. Take a slow step backward and pull them gently toward you. 3. Encourage them to look over their shoulder and take small steps in reverse.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent guiding child walking backward]

description: 1. Give the child a medium-sized playground ball. 2. Show them how to push the ball forward with two hands while walking. 3. Encourage them to keep the ball moving in a straight line toward a target.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pushing a ball while walking]

description: 1. Place a rattle in the child's open palm. 2. Gently close their fingers around the handle. 3. Encourage them to shake the rattle to hear the sound, reinforcing their grip strength.
activity_photo: [Image: Infant hand gripping a rattle]

description: 1. Sit with the child and a set of large blocks. 2. Place one block down and stack another on top. 3. Hand a block to the child and gesture for them to add it to the tower.
activity_photo: [Image: Child's hand stacking blocks]

description: 1. Provide a large plastic cup and several small safe objects (like large pom-poms). 2. Show the child how to pick up one object at a time. 3. Encourage them to drop the object into the cup and listen for the "plink."
activity_photo: [Image: Child dropping a ball into a cup]

description: 1. Place an empty bowl and a bowl filled with dry cereal side-by-side. 2. Give the child a chunky spoon. 3. Help them scoop the cereal and move it into the empty bowl.
activity_photo: [Image: Child moving items with a spoon]

description: 1. Use an extra-thick lace or a stiff pipe cleaner. 2. Hold a large bead with a wide hole. 3. Guide the child to push the lace through the hole and pull it out the other side.
activity_photo: [Image: Child threading a bead onto a string]

description: 1. Partially peel the edge of a large sticker from a sheet. 2. Show the child how to pinch the edge with their thumb and forefinger. 3. Encourage them to pull the sticker off and press it onto a piece of paper.
activity_photo: [Image: Child's fingers peeling a sticker]

description: 1. Give the child a golf-ball-sized piece of soft playdough. 2. Show them how to squeeze it tight in their fist so it oozes through their fingers. 3. Encourage them to poke it, squish it, and pull it apart.
activity_photo: [Image: Hand squeezing playdough]

description: 1. Tape a large piece of paper to the table to prevent sliding. 2. Give the child a thick "egg" or triangular crayon. 3. Demonstrate making a mark and encourage them to move their arm to make their own lines.
activity_photo: [Image: Child scribbling on paper]

description: 1. Use a jar with a slot cut into the lid. 2. Give the child large buttons (too big to swallow). 3. Show them how to orient the button vertically to fit it through the slot.
activity_photo: [Image: Child putting button in a jar slot]

description: 1. Give the child a strip of colorful tissue paper or thin construction paper. 2. Demonstrate holding the paper with both hands and pulling in opposite directions. 3. Encourage them to tear the paper into many small pieces.
activity_photo: [Image: Child's hands tearing paper]

description: 1. Clip several clothespins to the rim of a sturdy bowl. 2. Show the child how to squeeze the peg to open the "mouth." 3. Encourage them to pull the pegs off one by one and drop them into the bowl.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pinching a clothespin]

description: 1. Remove one piece from a large wooden knob puzzle. 2. Hand the piece to the child and point to the empty space. 3. Guide their hand to rotate and drop the piece into the matching slot.
activity_photo: [Image: Child fitting puzzle piece]

description: 1. Place a dollop of non-toxic paint on a large sheet of paper. 2. Show the child how to dip one finger into the paint. 3. Encourage them to smear, swirl, and make dots across the paper surface.
activity_photo: [Image: Child's hand covered in paint]

description: 1. Use a plastic piggy bank or a container with a thin slit. 2. Give the child large plastic play coins. 3. Show them how to line up the coin with the slot and push it all the way in.
activity_photo: [Image: Child inserting coin into slot]

description: 1. Draw a large, bold circle or square on a piece of paper. 2. Have the child dip their finger in water or paint. 3. Guide their finger to follow the lines of the shape from start to finish.
toy_photo: [Image: Paper with a large red circle]
activity_photo: [Image: Child's finger following a line]

description: 1. Poke several holes in the bottom of an upside-down colander. 2. Give the child colorful pipe cleaners. 3. Show them how to poke the end of the pipe cleaner into a hole and push it through.
activity_photo: [Image: Child poking wire into a hole]

description: 1. Place a mix of two different items (e.g., large pasta and blocks) in a pile. 2. Provide two separate containers. 3. Show the child how to pick up a block and put it in one container, then pasta in the other.
activity_photo: [Image: Child sorting items into bowls]

description: 1. Set out a set of graduated stacking cups. 2. Show the child how to place the largest cup down first. 3. Encourage them to find the next size and stack it precisely on top to build a tower.
activity_photo: [Image: Child building a cup tower]

description: 1. Stick several short strips of painter's tape to a high-chair tray or table. 2. Peel up one corner of each strip. 3. Encourage the child to use their "pincer grasp" to grab the corner and pull the tape off.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pulling tape off a table]

description: 1. Provide several small plastic containers with different types of lids (flip, pull, or screw). 2. Hide a small toy inside one. 3. Show the child how to remove the lid to find the toy, then help them put it back on.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pulling a lid off a tub]

description: 1. Scatter soft pom-poms on a flat surface. 2. Give the child a pair of large plastic tweezers or tongs. 3. Show them how to squeeze the tongs to grab a pom-pom and move it to a basket.
activity_photo: [Image: Child using tongs on a ball]

description: 1. Use toys or straps that have Velcro fasteners. 2. Close the Velcro firmly. 3. Encourage the child to grab the edge of the strap and pull hard to hear the "rrip" sound as it opens.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pulling a Velcro strap]

description: 1. Use a wooden board with large, secure pegs (Geoboard). 2. Show the child how to hook a thick rubber band onto one peg. 3. Encourage them to pull and stretch the band to hook it onto a second peg.
activity_photo: [Image: Child stretching a rubber band]

description: 1. Place a pegboard in front of the child. 2. Hand them one large plastic peg. 3. Point to a hole and guide them to push the peg down until it stays upright in the board.
activity_photo: [Image: Child inserting a peg into a board]

description: 1. Place one bowl filled with water and one empty bowl. 2. Put a small sponge in the water bowl. 3. Show the child how to move the wet sponge to the empty bowl and squeeze hard to release the water.
activity_photo: [Image: Child's hands squeezing a sponge]

description: 1. Use a "pop-up" toy or an activity center with buttons. 2. Point to a specific button. 3. Show the child how to use their pointer finger to push the button down to trigger a sound or a pop-up.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pressing a button]

description: 1. Sit with the child and a sturdy board book. 2. Show them how to slide their finger under the edge of the page. 3. Encourage them to turn one page at a time to see the next picture.
activity_photo: [Image: Child's hand turning a page]

description: 1. Remove all rings from a stacking post. 2. Hand the largest ring to the child. 3. Point to the post and encourage them to drop the ring over the top so it slides to the bottom.
activity_photo: [Image: Child placing a ring on a post]

description: 1. Give the child a sheet of newspaper or thin wrapping paper. 2. Show them how to use both hands to crush the paper into a small ball. 3. Encourage them to throw the "paper ball" into a basket.
activity_photo: [Image: Child's hands crushing paper]

description: 1. Provide a large toy nut and bolt set. 2. Hold the bolt steady for the child. 3. Show them how to twist the nut with their fingers to move it up or down the screw thread.
activity_photo: [Image: Child twisting a toy nut]

description: 1. Sit at eye level with the child so they can see your mouth clearly. 2. Speak slowly using exaggerated facial expressions and lip movements. 3. Pause frequently to give the child a chance to respond with a sound or facial movement.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent at eye-level talking to baby]

description: 1. Listen for a sound the child makes naturally (e.g., "ba"). 2. Repeat the exact sound back to them immediately. 3. Wait for them to make the sound again, creating a back-and-forth "conversation" of babbles.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent leaning in to listen to baby]

description: 1. Hold a familiar object like a "Ball" clearly in front of the child. 2. Say the name of the object twice: "Ball... Ball." 3. Encourage the child to look at the object and try to repeat the name or point to it.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent holding a shoe and naming it]

description: 1. Show the child a picture of a common animal (e.g., a cow). 2. Make the animal's sound clearly ("Moo!"). 3. Encourage the child to copy the sound whenever you point to that animal's picture.
tools: Animal picture book or toy animals
activity_photo: [Image: Child making a "moo" face with toy]

description: 1. Open a book with large, simple pictures. 2. Instead of reading the story, point to a picture and describe it: "Look at the big blue bird!" 3. Ask the child "Where is the bird?" and guide their hand to point to it.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent and child looking at a book]

description: 1. When the child wants something, use two-word phrases to describe it (e.g., "More juice" or "Blue ball"). 2. Encourage the child to attempt a second word by pausing after the first: "Want... [pause]... cookie?". 3. Celebrate any vocal attempt they make.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent holding a toy out to a child]

description: 1. Give the child a toy phone and take one for yourself. 2. Hold the phone to your ear and say "Hello? Is [Child's Name] there?". 3. Hand the phone to them and encourage them to "talk" and listen into the receiver.
activity_photo: [Image: Child holding toy phone to ear]

description: 1. Sing a short, simple song like "Twinkle Twinkle" several times. 2. Use the same hand gestures every time you sing it. 3. Eventually, stop singing at the end of a line (e.g., "How I wonder what you...") and wait for the child to fill in the last word.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent singing with hand motions]

description: 1. Point to your own nose and say "Nose." 2. Gently touch the child's nose and say "Your nose!". 3. Ask "Where is your nose?" and encourage them to point to their own or yours.
activity_photo: [Image: Child touching their own nose]

description: 1. Perform a simple action like "Jump" or "Clap." 2. Say the word as you do the action: "I am jumping!". 3. Encourage the child to do the same and say the word along with you.
activity_photo: [Image: Child jumping while parent says 'Jump']

description: 1. Ask simple "Yes/No" questions throughout the day (e.g., "Do you want water?"). 2. Exaggerate a nod for "Yes" and a shake for "No." 3. Wait for the child to respond with a gesture or a sound before providing the item.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent asking child a question]

description: 1. Say two words that rhyme clearly (e.g., "Cat, Hat"). 2. Repeat them with an emphasis on the ending sound. 3. Say a short rhyme and clap your hands on the rhyming words to draw the child's attention to the sound pattern.
toy_photo: [Image: Card with a cat and a hat]
activity_photo: [Image: Parent emphasizing sounds to child]

description: 1. Read a very familiar story to the child. 2. Turn to a page and ask "What happened here?". 3. Encourage the child to use one or two words to describe the picture or what comes next in the story.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pointing at a book page]

description: 1. Make a very happy face and say "I am happy!". 2. Use a mirror so the child can see their own face. 3. Ask them to "Make a happy face" and name the emotion they are showing.
activity_photo: [Image: Child looking in mirror making a face]

description: 1. Place a desired toy slightly out of reach but in plain sight. 2. Wait for the child to gesture or make a sound. 3. Prompt them by saying "What do you want?" and encourage them to use a word or point clearly before giving it to them.
activity_photo: [Image: Child reaching and vocalizing for toy]

description: 1. Put three different toys in front of the child (e.g., car, doll, ball). 2. Ask "Where is the car?". 3. Encourage the child to point to or pick up the correct toy, then say the name of the toy together.
toy_photo: [Image: A car, a doll, and a ball]
activity_photo: [Image: Child picking up a specific toy]

description: 1. Say a simple, fun word like "Pop!" or "Boom!". 2. Encourage the child to "echo" or repeat the word back to you. 3. Make it a game by changing the volume from a whisper to a loud voice and having them match you.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent and child shouting "Pop"]

description: 1. Sing a rhyme that has specific motions (e.g., "Itsy Bitsy Spider"). 2. Guide the child's hands to perform the movements as you sing. 3. Pause during the song to see if the child will start the next hand motion on their own.
activity_photo: [Image: Child doing spider hand motions]

description: 1. Hold up two different items (e.g., an apple and a banana). 2. Ask "Do you want the apple or the banana?". 3. Wait for the child to look at or point to their choice, then repeat the name of the chosen item clearly.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pointing to one of two items]

description: 1. Show a busy picture with many items (like a park scene). 2. Say "Find the doggie!". 3. Encourage the child to scan the picture and point to the correct object, then reward them with praise.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pointing to a detail in a book]

description: 1. Pick up a toy and point to a specific feature (e.g., "The car is red"). 2. Use simple sensory words like "soft," "loud," or "shiny" to describe it. 3. Encourage the child to touch the toy while you repeat the descriptive word.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent pointing at toy features]

description: 1. Hide behind a chair or door with an object that makes a distinct noise (like a bell). 2. Make the sound and ask, "What was that?". 3. Reveal the object, name it, and let the child make the sound themselves.
activity_photo: [Image: Child listening intently to a sound]

description: 1. Look through a photo album or digital pictures of family members. 2. Point to a person and ask "Who is that?". 3. Say the name (e.g., "Grandpa") and encourage the child to repeat it or wave at the picture.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pointing at a photo]

description: 1. Place a toy in an obvious but slightly hidden spot (e.g., under a clear cloth). 2. Ask the child, "Where is your teddy?". 3. Encourage them to look around and point to or crawl toward the object.
activity_photo: [Image: Child searching around the room]

description: 1. Say a simple, silly sound or a word (e.g., "Beep-beep!"). 2. Look at the child expectantly and wait for them to try and mimic you. 3. Gradually increase the difficulty to two-word phrases once they master single sounds.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent and child face-to-face]

description: 1. Sing a very familiar nursery rhyme with a strong rhythm. 2. Stop abruptly before a rhyming word or a key phrase (e.g., "The wheels on the bus go round and..."). 3. Wait for the child to finish the line with a sound, word, or gesture.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent pausing mid-song]

description: 1. Narrate what you are doing during a daily task like diapering or dressing. 2. Use simple sentences: "Now we put on your sock. One sock, two socks." 3. Pause to see if the child anticipates the next step by looking or moving.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent talking while dressing child]

description: 1. Walk around the house and listen for specific sounds (a ticking clock, a bird, a running tap). 2. Point to your ear and say "Listen! I hear a..." 3. Lead the child to the source of the sound and name the object making it.
activity_photo: [Image: Child with hand to ear listening]

description: 1. When the child says a single word (e.g., "Dog"), repeat it back and add a word. 2. Say, "Yes, big dog!" or "Brown dog!". 3. This helps the child learn how to combine words into short phrases.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent nodding and talking to child]

description: 1. Sit with the child in front of a large mirror. 2. Make funny faces or stick out your tongue and describe the action. 3. Encourage the child to "talk" to their reflection and watch how their mouth moves.
activity_photo: [Image: Child babbling at their reflection]

description: 1. Hold a black-and-white high-contrast card about 8-12 inches from the infant's face. 2. Slowly move the card from side to side. 3. Watch as the child tracks the bold patterns, which helps develop visual focus and brain connections.
activity_photo: [Image: Infant tracking a card]

description: 1. Hide your face behind your hands or a scarf. 2. Ask "Where is Mama/Papa?" in an excited voice. 3. Quickly reveal your face and say "Peekaboo!" to teach that things exist even when unseen.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent revealing face behind hands]

description: 1. Show the child a toy, then hide it completely under a small blanket while they watch. 2. Ask "Where did it go?". 3. Encourage the child to lift the blanket to find the toy, building memory and persistence.
activity_photo: [Image: Child lifting a blanket to find toy]

description: 1. Present a shape sorter with only one type of hole open (e.g., the circle). 2. Hand the child the matching shape. 3. Guide their hand to align the shape and push it through the hole.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pushing shape into sorter]

description: 1. Use two bowls of different colors (e.g., Red and Blue). 2. Provide several red and blue blocks. 3. Show the child how to "match" the red block to the red bowl, then encourage them to try.
activity_photo: [Image: Child placing block in matching bowl]

description: 1. Use a puzzle with only 2 or 3 large pieces. 2. Remove the pieces and show the child the empty board. 3. Encourage them to fit the pieces back by matching the shapes and pictures.
activity_photo: [Image: Child assembling a 2-piece puzzle]

description: 1. Lay out two pairs of identical cards face up. 2. Point to one and ask the child to "find the one just like this." 3. Encourage them to pick up the matching card, reinforcing visual memory.
activity_photo: [Image: Child holding two matching cards]

description: 1. Use nesting cups or rings of different sizes. 2. Show the child that the small one fits inside the big one. 3. Encourage them to experiment with the order to see which ones fit together and which ones don't.
activity_photo: [Image: Child trying to fit cups together]

description: 1. Present a toy that reacts to an action (e.g., a jack-in-the-box or a button that makes a light flash). 2. Demonstrate the action clearly. 3. Encourage the child to repeat the action to get the same fun result.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pressing a button for light]

description: 1. Safely hold the child near a light switch. 2. Say "Lights ON" as you flip it up, and "Lights OFF" as you flip it down. 3. Let the child try to move the switch themselves to see the immediate change in the room.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent holding child to reach switch]

description: 1. Fill a basket with various items like blocks, socks, and spoons. 2. Set out three empty containers. 3. Show the child how to put all the blocks in one, socks in the second, and spoons in the third.
activity_photo: [Image: Child sorting items into three bins]

description: 1. Place two different colored blocks in a row (e.g., Red, Blue). 2. Hand the child a red block and a blue block. 3. Encourage them to place their blocks in the same order next to yours.
toy_photo: [Image: Red and blue blocks in a line]
activity_photo: [Image: Child mimicking a block pattern]

description: 1. Line up 3-5 large items like toy cars. 2. Touch each item one by one as you say the number clearly: "One, two, three..." 3. Encourage the child to touch the items along with you as you count.
toy_photo: [Image: Five toy cars in a row]
activity_photo: [Image: Finger touching a toy while counting]

description: 1. Lay out three different picture cards (e.g., Apple, Dog, Sun). 2. Hand the child a duplicate "Apple" card. 3. Ask them to "Find the one that looks like this" and place it on top of the matching card.
activity_photo: [Image: Child matching two identical cards]

description: 1. Hide a noisy toy (like a ticking timer or music box) under a pillow. 2. Ask the child "Where is the music coming from?". 3. Encourage them to follow the sound and lift the pillow to reveal the "treasure".
activity_photo: [Image: Child listening for a hidden toy]

description: 1. Scatter several toys of different colors on the floor. 2. Ask the child "Can you find something red?". 3. Praise them when they pick up a red item and name the color again to reinforce the concept.
activity_photo: [Image: Child holding up a red toy]

description: 1. Build a tall tower of soft blocks in front of the child. 2. Say "1, 2, 3... Knock it down!". 3. Let the child push the tower over, then encourage them to help you rebuild it to learn cause and effect.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pushing over a block tower]

description: 1. Mix toy animals and toy vehicles in a pile. 2. Label two boxes: "Animals" and "Cars." 3. Show the child how to sort them, explaining that one group has legs and the other has wheels.
toy_photo: [Image: Toy cow and toy truck side-by-side]
activity_photo: [Image: Child placing a cow in an animal bin]

description: 1. Give the child 5 blocks and keep 5 for yourself. 2. Tell them "Let's see how high we can go!". 3. Take turns adding one block at a time to a single tower, teaching patience and steady hand movements.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent and child adding to a tower]

description: 1. Place three familiar toys on a tray (e.g., Ball, Cup, Spoon). 2. Have the child close their eyes, then remove one toy. 3. Ask "What is gone?" and encourage them to remember the missing item.
activity_photo: [Image: Child looking at a tray with one empty spot]

description: 1. Draw the outlines (shadows) of 3 simple toys on a piece of paper. 2. Hand the child the actual toys. 3. Encourage them to place each toy onto its corresponding "shadow" drawing.
activity_photo: [Image: Child placing a toy on its outline]

description: 1. Provide a large empty bucket and a scoop of dry rice or sand. 2. Show the child how to fill the bucket to the top. 3. Then, show them how to pour it all out to understand concepts of "full" and "empty".
activity_photo: [Image: Child pouring rice from a scoop]

description: 1. Hold up a large ball and a very small ball. 2. Ask the child "Which one is BIG?". 3. Encourage them to point to or grab the larger object, then repeat the word "Big".
tools: One large ball, one small ball
toy_photo: [Image: Large beach ball and small tennis ball]
activity_photo: [Image: Child pointing to a large object]

description: 1. Lay out a sequence of activities (e.g., Brush hair, then put on hat). 2. Show the child the two steps in order. 3. Ask them "What do we do first?" and guide them through the simple two-step routine.
activity_photo: [Image: Child brushing hair then reaching for hat]

description: 1. Place a small toy under one of two identical cups while the child watches. 2. Slowly move the cups around. 3. Ask "Where is the toy?" and let the child lift a cup to find it.
tools: Two identical plastic cups, small toy
activity_photo: [Image: Child lifting a cup to find a toy]

description: 1. Clap a simple rhythm (e.g., Clap-Clap, Pause). 2. Look at the child and say "Your turn!". 3. Encourage them to mimic the same rhythm, helping them develop auditory memory.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent and child clapping together]

description: 1. Stand behind the child and make a sound (e.g., shake a bell or crinkle paper). 2. Ask "Where is that sound?". 3. Encourage the child to turn their head or point in the direction the sound came from.
activity_photo: [Image: Child turning head toward a sound]

description: 1. Give a simple command with two parts: "Pick up the ball and put it in the box." 2. Wait for the child to process both steps. 3. Praise them for completing the sequence in the correct order.
activity_photo: [Image: Child placing a ball into a box]

description: 1. Scatter 3 pairs of identical socks on the floor. 2. Pick up one sock and show it to the child. 3. Ask "Can you find the other one just like this?" to encourage visual matching.
activity_photo: [Image: Child holding two matching socks]

description: 1. Draw a wide, simple path on a piece of paper leading from a "Start" to a "Finish" (e.g., a mouse to a cheese). 2. Show the child how to move their finger along the path. 3. Encourage them to stay "inside the lines" until the end.
activity_photo: [Image: Child tracing a line with their finger]

description: 1. Sit with the child in front of a mirror. 2. Make a big, bright smile and say "Happy!". 3. Wait for the child to see your reflection and encourage them to smile back at themselves and you.
activity_photo: [Image: Child smiling at their reflection]

description: 1. Sit facing the child and start a slow, rhythmic clap. 2. Reach out and gently help the child clap their hands together. 3. Cheer and laugh together to celebrate the shared rhythmic movement.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent and child clapping together]

description: 1. Sit on the floor across from the child. 2. Roll a soft ball to them and say "Your turn!". 3. Wait for them to roll it back and say "My turn!", teaching the flow of social play.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent and child rolling a ball]

description: 1. Give the child a doll or teddy bear and a toy spoon. 2. Show them how to "feed" the doll. 3. Encourage the child to mimic the nurturing action, fostering early empathy.
activity_photo: [Image: Child "feeding" a teddy bear]

description: 1. Play with a set of blocks together. 2. Hand a block to the child and say "One for you." 3. Ask the child to "Give one to me," praising them when they hand a toy over.
activity_photo: [Image: Child handing a toy to a parent]

description: 1. Sit in a circle with family or other children. 2. Sing a familiar song with hand motions like "If You're Happy and You Know It." 3. Encourage the child to look at others and join in the collective movements.
activity_photo: [Image: Children sitting in a circle singing]

description: 1. Make an exaggerated face (Happy, Sad, Surprised). 2. Name the emotion clearly: "I am sad." 3. Ask the child to copy your face and name the feeling together.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent and child making funny faces]

description: 1. When someone leaves the room, say "Bye-bye!". 2. Demonstrate a waving motion with your hand. 3. Help the child lift their hand and wave to practice social greetings and departures.
activity_photo: [Image: Child waving at a door]

description: 1. Open your arms wide and say "Hug?". 2. Lean in for a gentle embrace. 3. Encourage the child to initiate hugs with you or a favorite stuffed animal to express affection.
activity_photo: [Image: Child hugging a parent]

description: 1. Sit behind or to the side of the child while they play. 2. Call their name clearly in a cheerful voice. 3. Reward them with a smile or a tickle the moment they turn their head to acknowledge you.
activity_photo: [Image: Child turning head when called]

description: 1. Provide a toy pot and a wooden spoon. 2. Show the child how to "stir" the pot. 3. Pretend to taste the "food" and say "Mmm, yummy!" to encourage imaginative role-play.
activity_photo: [Image: Child stirring a toy pot]

description: 1. Set out a basket of easy-to-wear items like large hats or scarves. 2. Put a hat on yourself, then on the child. 3. Look in the mirror together and talk about the "new" characters you've become.
activity_photo: [Image: Child wearing a large adult hat]

description: 1. Say "I'm gonna get you!" in a playful tone. 2. Gently tickle the child's tummy or toes. 3. Pause and wait for their laughter or a "more" gesture before continuing to build social anticipation.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent tickling a laughing child]

description: 1. When a family member enters, say "Hello!". 2. Encourage the child to look at the person. 3. Prompt the child to wave or say a sound to acknowledge the arrival of a loved one.
activity_photo: [Image: Child reaching for a person entering]

description: 1. Read a book where a character is feeling an emotion. 2. Point to the character's face and say, "He is happy because he has a ball." 3. Ask the child "Are you happy?" to bridge the story to their own feelings.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent and child discussing a book]

description: 1. Hand a toy to the child and say "Here you go." 2. When the child hands you something, say "Thank you" with a big smile. 3. Model the behavior consistently to help the child learn the social rhythm of gratitude.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent smiling while receiving a toy]

description: 1. Hold your palm up and say "High Five!". 2. Guide the child's hand to slap yours. 3. Celebrate the contact with a cheer to build a sense of shared accomplishment.
activity_photo: [Image: Child giving parent a high five]

description: 1. Hold a toy and offer it to the child. 2. Once they take it, gently ask "Can I have it please?". 3. When they give it back, praise them immediately to encourage the flow of reciprocal play.
activity_photo: [Image: Child handing a toy back to parent]

description: 1. Show the child a photo of a family member who isn't present. 2. Name the person and talk about them: "That's Grandma! She loves you." 3. Encourage the child to kiss the photo or wave to foster long-distance bonding.
activity_photo: [Image: Child looking at a family photo]

description: 1. Lay a teddy bear down and cover it with a small cloth. 2. Whisper "Shh, teddy is sleeping." 3. Have the child "pat" the bear gently to practice being quiet and careful with others.
activity_photo: [Image: Child patting a stuffed animal]

description: 1. When someone enters the room, say "Hello!" in a cheerful voice. 2. Demonstrate a waving motion. 3. Encourage the child to look at the person and mirror your wave to practice social greetings.
activity_photo: [Image: Child waving at an open door]

description: 1. Play a favorite upbeat song. 2. Hold the child's hands and bounce or sway together. 3. Laugh and cheer as you move, showing the child how to express joy through physical movement.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent and child dancing together]

description: 1. Identify a specific soft toy the child gravitates toward when tired or upset. 2. Offer the toy during quiet transitions or naps. 3. Use the toy to model self-soothing by hugging it yourself first.
activity_photo: [Image: Child cuddling a plush toy]

description: 1. Make a funny sound or a silly face (e.g., a "pop" sound with your cheek). 2. Wait for the child to react. 3. Repeat the action that made them laugh to build a shared sense of humor and connection.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent and child laughing]

description: 1. Hold a large but lightweight toy (like a beach ball). 2. Ask the child "Can you help me?". 3. Have them hold one side while you hold the other as you move it across the room.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent and child carrying a box]

description: 1. Set out a few toy food items and a small basket. 2. Pretend to pick an item and put it in the basket. 3. Encourage the child to "shop" and hand you items to "buy," practicing social exchange.
activity_photo: [Image: Child placing toy food in basket]

description: 1. Use a toy stethoscope to "listen" to a teddy bear's heart. 2. Gently show the child how to do the same. 3. This reduces anxiety about real check-ups and encourages nurturing behavior.
activity_photo: [Image: Child using toy on a teddy bear]

description: 1. Place a few small crackers on a plate. 2. Take one and say "One for me." 3. Hand one to the child and say "One for you," teaching the basics of fair distribution and sharing.
activity_photo: [Image: Child and parent sharing a snack]

description: 1. Use two dolls to act out a simple interaction, like waving "Hi." 2. Give one doll to the child and keep one for yourself. 3. Encourage the dolls to "talk" or play together to model friendship.
activity_photo: [Image: Child playing with two dolls]

description: 1. Lean close to the child and wait for them to look at you. 2. Give a big, warm smile and wait silently. 3. When they smile back, respond with a verbal "I see that big smile!" to reinforce emotional bonding.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent and baby smiling at each other]

description: 1. Use a small amount of baby-safe oil or lotion. 2. Gently stroke the child's arms and legs with firm but soft pressure. 3. Narrate the touch (e.g., "Soft touch on your toes") to help them process tactile input.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent massaging a baby's leg]

description: 1. Fill a low basket with items like silk, a loofah, a smooth stone, and a pinecone. 2. Encourage the child to reach in and explore. 3. Use words like "rough," "smooth," or "fuzzy" as they touch each item.
activity_photo: [Image: Child feeling a bumpy ball]

description: 1. Fill a shallow tray with an inch of water. 2. Show the child how to tap the surface to make a splash. 3. Add a few floating toys to encourage them to reach and move their hands through the water.
activity_photo: [Image: Child splashing water in a tub]

description: 1. Fill a large plastic bin with dry rice. 2. Bury several small plastic toys under the rice. 3. Encourage the child to use their hands to "dig" through the rice and find the hidden treasures.
tools: Large bin, dry rice, small toys
activity_photo: [Image: Child's hands buried in rice]

description: 1. Provide a small tray of clean play sand. 2. Show the child how to run their fingers through it or squeeze it. 3. Use a small rake or cup to show how the sand moves and takes shape.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pouring sand from a cup]

description: 1. Roll out a flat "pancake" of playdough. 2. Give the child items like shells or large buttons. 3. Show them how to press the items into the dough to leave an impression, then peel them off.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pressing a hand into dough]

description: 1. Blow a few bubbles into the air toward the child. 2. Encourage them to watch the bubbles move and track them with their eyes. 3. Show them how to reach out and "catch" a bubble on their hand before it pops.
activity_photo: [Image: Child reaching for a bubble]

description: 1. Use a large, soft craft feather. 2. Gently brush the feather against the child's palm, arm, or cheek. 3. Observe their reaction to the light, ticklish sensation and name the feeling ("That's soft!").
activity_photo: [Image: Parent brushing a feather on child's hand]

description: 1. Place a few large ice cubes in a bowl. 2. Let the child touch the ice for a few seconds. 3. Talk about the sensation of "Cold!" and watch how the ice slips and melts in their hand.
toy_photo: [Image: Clear ice cubes in a bowl]
activity_photo: [Image: Child touching a cold ice cube]

description: 1. Provide two plastic cups, one filled with water. 2. Show the child how to pour water from one cup into the other. 3. Listen to the "glug-glug" sound and watch the water move to build hand-eye coordination.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pouring water into a tray]

description: 1. Lay out different "floor stations" using a rug, a towel, and bubble wrap. 2. Hold the child's hands as they walk barefoot over each surface. 3. Describe the change in feeling, such as "soft," "bumpy," or "scratchy."
activity_photo: [Image: Child walking on bubble wrap]

description: 1. Fill three identical plastic eggs with different items (beans, rice, a bell). 2. Shake one egg and listen to the unique sound it makes. 3. Encourage the child to shake the eggs and find the one that sounds "loud" or "quiet."
activity_photo: [Image: Child shaking a plastic egg]

description: 1. Dim the lights and shine a flashlight against a plain wall. 2. Move your hand in front of the light to create shadows. 3. Encourage the child to try and "catch" the shadow on the wall with their hands.
activity_photo: [Image: Hand shadow on a wall]

description: 1. Hold a safe, scented item like a lemon slice or a cinnamon stick near the child. 2. Say "Mmm, smell the lemon!" and take a deep breath. 3. Observe the child's reaction as they take a sniff of the new scent.
activity_photo: [Image: Child smelling a piece of fruit]

description: 1. Turn on a small electric fan on a low setting. 2. Hold a lightweight scarf in front of the fan so it flutters. 3. Let the child feel the air on their skin and watch how the wind moves the fabric.
activity_photo: [Image: Child feeling air from a fan]

description: 1. Prepare a bowl of comfortably warm water (test on your wrist first). 2. Let the child dip their hands or feet into the water. 3. Talk about the "warm" sensation compared to the cool air in the room.
activity_photo: [Image: Child's feet in warm water]

description: 1. Place a metal spoon in the refrigerator for 10 minutes. 2. Gently touch the back of the cold spoon to the child’s palm or cheek. 3. Watch for their reaction to the sudden temperature change and say "Ooh, cold!".
activity_photo: [Image: Parent touching spoon to child's hand]

description: 1. Spray a small amount of unscented shaving foam or whipped cream onto a tray. 2. Show the child how to draw lines or circles in the foam with their finger. 3. Encourage them to squish the foam between their hands to feel the airy texture.
activity_photo: [Image: Child drawing in foam on a tray]

description: 1. Spread a thin layer of sand over a dark-colored tray. 2. Use your finger to draw a simple shape or a letter. 3. Have the child "erase" the drawing by shaking the tray and then let them draw their own lines.
toy_photo: [Image: Tray with a layer of sand]
activity_photo: [Image: Finger drawing a circle in sand]

description: 1. Collect several leaves of different shapes and textures (crunchy, smooth, fuzzy). 2. Let the child hold and crumble a dry leaf to hear the sound. 3. Compare it to a smooth green leaf to explore natural textures.
activity_photo: [Image: Child crumbling a dry leaf]

description: 1. Take the child to a patch of clean, safe grass. 2. Let them stand or crawl barefoot on the grass. 3. Describe the feeling of the "tickly" grass on their skin as they move around.
activity_photo: [Image: Child crawling on grass]

description: 1. Blow bubbles upward so they float down toward the child. 2. Encourage the child to use their "pointer finger" to poke a bubble. 3. Celebrate with a "Pop!" sound every time they successfully touch one.
activity_photo: [Image: Child's finger popping a bubble]

description: 1. Gather scraps of different fabrics like corduroy, satin, and fleece. 2. Rub a piece gently against the child's arm. 3. Let them grab the fabric and feel the difference between the "bumpy" and "soft" materials.
activity_photo: [Image: Child feeling a piece of satin]

description: 1. Use a sponge or a washcloth soaked in water. 2. Hold it above a bowl and squeeze it slowly so the water drips. 3. Encourage the child to watch the drops fall and listen to the "plop" sound in the water.
activity_photo: [Image: Water dripping into a bowl]

description: 1. Use a ball with a unique texture (e.g., a nubby sensory ball). 2. Roll the ball slowly over the child's legs or back. 3. Encourage them to catch the ball and explore the "bumps" with their own hands.
activity_photo: [Image: Ball being rolled on child's arm]

description: 1. Use a toy that gently vibrates when a string is pulled or a button is pushed. 2. Place the vibrating toy against the child's hand. 3. Observe their curiosity as they feel the steady buzzing sensation.
activity_photo: [Image: Child holding a vibrating toy]

description: 1. Tape squares of different materials (tinfoil, felt, cardboard) to the floor in a line. 2. Encourage the child to crawl along the path. 3. Notice how they react to the "crinkle" of the foil versus the "soft" felt.
activity_photo: [Image: Child crawling on tinfoil]

description: 1. Mix corn flour with a little water to create "Oobleck" (a goop that is both solid and liquid). 2. Let the child punch the surface, then watch their hand sink in. 3. Show them how to scoop it up and watch it "melt" through their fingers.
toy_photo: [Image: Bowl of white corn flour goop]
activity_photo: [Image: Child's hands in white goop]

description: 1. Fill small plastic bottles with different amounts of water. 2. Shake the bottles to show how the sound changes based on the water level. 3. Let the child shake them to feel the weight shift and hear the splashing.
activity_photo: [Image: Child shaking a water bottle]

description: 1. Use a very soft makeup brush or a baby hairbrush. 2. Gently "paint" the child’s hand or foot with the dry bristles. 3. Describe the sensation as "tickly" or "soft" to build sensory vocabulary.
tools: Soft baby brush or makeup brush
activity_photo: [Image: Parent brushing child's foot]

description: 1. Place small, soft pieces of food (like steamed carrots) on a high-chair tray. 2. Show the child how to pick up one piece using their thumb and forefinger. 3. Encourage them to bring the food to their mouth independently.
activity_photo: [Image: Child picking up a small snack]

description: 1. Use a small, open cup with a tiny amount of water. 2. Guide the child's hands to hold both sides of the cup. 3. Help them tip it slowly to take a small sip without spilling.
activity_photo: [Image: Child holding cup to mouth]

description: 1. At the end of play, bring a large bin to the center of the room. 2. Pick up a toy and say "In the box!". 3. Hand a toy to the child and guide them to drop it into the bin.
activity_photo: [Image: Child putting a doll in a box]

description: 1. Loosen the heel of the child's sock slightly. 2. Show them how to grab the toe part of the sock. 3. Encourage them to pull the sock all the way off their foot.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pulling a sock off]

description: 1. Stand the child at the sink using a secure step stool. 2. Apply a small drop of mild soap to their hands. 3. Help them rub their palms together and rinse under the water.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent helping child wash hands]

description: 1. Apply a smear of child-safe toothpaste to a small brush. 2. Let the child hold the handle while you guide the bristles over their teeth. 3. Allow them to "brush" on their own for a few seconds to build familiarity.
activity_photo: [Image: Child holding a toothbrush]

description: 1. Provide a bowl of thick food (like yogurt or oatmeal) that stays on a spoon. 2. Scoop a small amount and hand the spoon to the child. 3. Guide their hand to their mouth to help them learn the scooping motion.
activity_photo: [Image: Child trying to feed themselves]

description: 1. Place a soft, loose hat on the child's head while looking in a mirror. 2. Show them how to grab the brim and pull it off. 3. Encourage them to try and "plop" the hat back onto their head.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pulling a hat off]

description: 1. Hold out a shirt with a wide neck opening. 2. Encourage the child to push their arms through the sleeve holes. 3. Praise their effort as they help pull the garment down over their tummy.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pushing arm through sleeve]

description: 1. After washing hands, hand a small, soft towel to the child. 2. Show them how to rub the towel over their wet hands. 3. Encourage them to "pat-pat" their skin until the water is gone.
activity_photo: [Image: Child rubbing hands with a towel]

description: 1. Identify a low, open shelf where a specific toy belongs. 2. Hand the toy to the child and point to the shelf. 3. Guide them to walk over and place the toy neatly in its "home."
activity_photo: [Image: Child placing a toy on a shelf]

description: 1. Place a few dry crackers on a lightweight, non-slip plastic plate. 2. Have the child hold the plate with both hands. 3. Encourage them to walk a short distance to the table without dropping the crackers.
activity_photo: [Image: Child carrying a plate carefully]

description: 1. Provide a child-safe water bottle with a straw or spout. 2. Show them how to flip the lid or position the straw. 3. Encourage them to hold the bottle and drink independently throughout the day.
activity_photo: [Image: Child drinking from a straw]

description: 1. Place a sturdy, child-sized chair near the child. 2. Show them how to turn around and back up toward the seat. 3. Assist them in lowering themselves safely into the chair to sit.
activity_photo: [Image: Child sitting down in a small chair]

description: 1. After a nap, lay the child's small blanket flat on the floor. 2. Show them how to take two corners and bring them to the middle. 3. Encourage them to "smooth" the blanket with their hands.
activity_photo: [Image: Child's hands folding fabric]

description: 1. Designate a specific spot or mat near the door for shoes. 2. Hand the child their shoes after coming inside. 3. Encourage them to bend down and place the shoes neatly on the designated spot.
activity_photo: [Image: Child placing shoes on a mat]

description: 1. Give the child a small piece of clean laundry (like a sock). 2. Point to the laundry basket. 3. Encourage them to walk over and drop the item into the basket to "help" with chores.
activity_photo: [Image: Child dropping a sock in a basket]

description: 1. After a meal, show the child your empty spoon. 2. Guide them to a low plastic basin or the kitchen sink. 3. Encourage them to drop their used spoon into the basin to signal the end of the meal.
activity_photo: [Image: Child putting a spoon in a tub]

description: 1. Give the child a small, safe piece of trash (like a paper scrap). 2. Point to a small, open wastebasket. 3. Encourage them to drop the paper inside and say "All gone!".
activity_photo: [Image: Child dropping paper in a bin]

description: 1. Place a very light item (like a plush toy) in a small tote bag. 2. Hand the handle of the bag to the child. 3. Encourage them to carry the bag while walking from one room to another.
activity_photo: [Image: Child walking with a small bag]

description: 1. Hand the child a sturdy board book. 2. Point to a low, reachable shelf. 3. Guide them to slide the book onto the shelf alongside others.
activity_photo: [Image: Child placing a book on a shelf]

description: 1. Give the child a small, damp microfiber cloth. 2. Demonstrate a circular wiping motion on a low table. 3. Encourage them to "clean up" their play surface.
activity_photo: [Image: Child wiping a table]

description: 1. Point to scattered toys on the floor. 2. Hand one toy to the child and gesture toward the box. 3. Celebrate every toy they successfully put inside the container.
activity_photo: [Image: Child cleaning up toys]

description: 1. Open a low, safe drawer (e.g., in a play kitchen). 2. Show the child how to place their palms flat on the front. 3. Encourage them to push until the drawer clicks shut.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pushing a drawer shut]

description: 1. After drinking, guide the child to hold their cup with both hands. 2. Point to a flat, clear spot on the table. 3. Encourage them to set the cup down gently without tipping it over.
activity_photo: [Image: Child placing cup on a table]

description: 1. Drop a clean washcloth or napkin on the floor. 2. Ask the child "Can you get that?". 3. Encourage them to bend their knees, pick up the cloth, and hand it to you.
activity_photo: [Image: Child bending to pick up cloth]

description: 1. Provide an easy-to-open lunch box with a simple latch. 2. Show the child how to lift the clip. 3. Encourage them to pull the lid open to find a small treat or toy inside.
activity_photo: [Image: Child lifting a lunch box lid]

description: 1. During a meal, hand the child a clean paper or cloth napkin. 2. Show them how to hold it in their lap or hand. 3. Encourage them to use it to "pat" their mouth after eating.
activity_photo: [Image: Child holding a napkin]

description: 1. When entering the house, point to a specific shoe rack or mat. 2. Assist the child in taking off their shoes. 3. Encourage them to carry the shoes over and set them down in the designated "shoe home".
activity_photo: [Image: Child setting shoes on a mat]

description: 1. Lay a small square washcloth flat. 2. Show the child how to bring two corners together to make a rectangle. 3. Help them press down on the fold with their palm to make it "neat".
activity_photo: [Image: Child folding a cloth]

description: 1. Dim the room lights. 2. Shine a flashlight on the wall about two feet from the child. 3. Slowly move the light beam in a circle or zig-zag, allowing the child to track the light with their eyes.
activity_photo: [Image: Infant watching a light spot on the wall]

description: 1. Sit eye-to-eye with the child. 2. Make distinct mouth movements like blowing bubbles, smacking lips, or sticking out your tongue. 3. Pause and wait for the child to attempt to move their mouth in the same way.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent blowing a raspberry at infant]

description: 1. Place several bright sticky notes at various heights on walls and furniture. 2. Encourage the child to walk or crawl to each note. 3. Have them use their fingers to peel the note off the surface and collect them.
activity_photo: [Image: Child peeling a yellow note off a wall]

description: 1. Arch your body over the child like a bridge. 2. Place a toy on the other side of your body. 3. Encourage the child to crawl through the narrow space under you to reach the toy.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent arching over crawling child]

description: 1. Stuff several small pom-poms or fabric scraps inside a metal kitchen whisk. 2. Hand it to the child. 3. Show them how to use their fingers to pull the items out through the wire gaps.
toy_photo: [Image: Metal whisk with colorful pom-poms inside]
activity_photo: [Image: Child pulling fabric out of a whisk]

description: 1. Mix safe scents like vanilla or peppermint into homemade dough. 2. Have the child squeeze the dough. 3. Bring it near their nose and describe the scent (e.g., 'sweet' or 'cool').
toy_photo: [Image: Ball of dough with a vanilla bean]
activity_photo: [Image: Child smelling a ball of dough]

description: 1. Freeze water mixed with food coloring in an ice tray. 2. Place a large sheet of paper on a tray. 3. Let the child hold the colored ice cube and slide it across the paper as it melts to create art.
activity_photo: [Image: Child drawing with a melting ice cube]

description: 1. Drape a large bedsheet over two chairs to create a low tunnel. 2. Place a mirror at the end. 3. Encourage the child to navigate the darkened space to reach their reflection.
activity_photo: [Image: Child crawling under a draped sheet]

description: 1. Squirt two different colors of paint (e.g., yellow and blue) into a sealable plastic bag. 2. Tape the bag firmly to a table or window. 3. Encourage the child to press and move the paint with their fingers to see a new color appear.
toy_photo: [Image: Bag with yellow and blue paint]
activity_photo: [Image: Child's hand squishing paint in a bag]

description: 1. Place one bowl full of water and one empty bowl side by side. 2. Give the child a large sponge. 3. Show them how to soak the sponge, move it to the empty bowl, and squeeze the water out.
activity_photo: [Image: Child squeezing water into a bowl]

description: 1. On a sunny day, place a piece of paper on the ground near a tree or plant. 2. Position a toy so its shadow falls on the paper. 3. Help the child move a crayon along the edges of the shadow.
activity_photo: [Image: Child tracing a shadow on paper]

description: 1. Mix up 4-5 pairs of distinct socks in a pile. 2. Pick up one sock and show it to the child. 3. Ask them to find the 'friend' that looks exactly the same.
activity_photo: [Image: Child holding two identical striped socks]

description: 1. Provide a muffin tin and a variety of small objects (large buttons, shells, blocks). 2. Assign one type of object to each 'cup'. 3. Encourage the child to sort the remaining items into the correct holes.
activity_photo: [Image: Child placing buttons in muffin cups]

description: 1. Provide two identical pieces of fabric (like washcloths). 2. Dip one in water and leave the other dry. 3. Have the child touch both and use words like 'wet' and 'dry' to describe the difference.
toy_photo: [Image: One folded dry cloth, one damp cloth]
activity_photo: [Image: Child touching a wet cloth with curiosity]

description: 1. In a slightly darkened room, ask the child to find a specific object (e.g., 'Find the red bear'). 2. Give them a flashlight to shine around the room. 3. Celebrate when the light beam lands on the correct object.
toy_photo: [Image: Beam of light hitting a teddy bear]
activity_photo: [Image: Child pointing flashlight at a toy]

description: 1. Fill one small box with heavy books and another with crumpled paper. 2. Tape both shut. 3. Ask the child to push or lift each box to feel the difference in effort required.
activity_photo: [Image: Child straining to lift a heavy box]

description: 1. Gently fasten a soft wrist rattle or a small bell on a soft ribbon around the infant's ankle. 2. Lay them on their back. 3. As they move their legs, the sound will play, encouraging them to kick more to hear the chime.
activity_photo: [Image: Infant kicking leg with a rattle attached]

description: 1. Place a light craft feather on a flat table. 2. Show the child how to blow air through their mouth to move the feather. 3. See how far they can move the feather across the table with one big breath.
activity_photo: [Image: Child leaning over to blow a feather]

description: 1. Set out a bowl of large pom-poms and an empty plastic bottle. 2. Give the child a pair of kitchen tongs. 3. Encourage them to pick up a pom-pom with the tongs and drop it into the narrow mouth of the bottle.
activity_photo: [Image: Child concentrating on moving a pom-pom]

description: 1. Sit facing the child. 2. Perform a simple action like touching your ears or clapping once. 3. Tell the child 'Be my mirror' and have them repeat the action immediately.
toy_photo: [Image: Icon of two faces facing each other]
activity_photo: [Image: Child touching ears after parent does]

description: 1. Lay a sturdy blanket on the floor and place the infant in the center. 2. Two adults grab the corners of the blanket and gently lift it slightly off the ground. 3. Slowly swing the blanket side to side to help the child get used to gentle motion.
activity_photo: [Image: Two adults gently swinging a baby in a blanket]

description: 1. Lay the child on a soft carpet or grassy patch with their arms at their sides. 2. Show them how to roll their body sideways like a log. 3. Encourage them to roll from one end of the room to the other to stimulate their balance centers.
activity_photo: [Image: Child rolling horizontally on a mat]

description: 1. Sit in a chair and place the infant on your lap facing you. 2. Hold them securely under the arms. 3. Bounce your heels up and down rhythmically while making a fun sound or singing a song.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent bouncing smiling baby on lap]

description: 1. Place a large, flat, slightly squishy floor pillow on the ground. 2. Hold the child's hand for stability. 3. Encourage them to stand and walk across the soft, uneven surface to challenge their balance.
activity_photo: [Image: Child wobbling while walking on a cushion]

description: 1. Have the child sit securely inside a large, smooth laundry basket. 2. Hold the edges of the basket firmly. 3. Slowly spin the basket in a circle a few times, then stop to let them process the dizziness.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent spinning child sitting in a basket]

description: 1. Turn a few metal and plastic pots upside down on the floor. 2. Give the child a wooden spoon. 3. Show them how to tap the different pots to hear the variations in sound and rhythm.
toy_photo: [Image: Assorted kitchen pots and wooden spoon]
activity_photo: [Image: Child hitting a pot with a wooden spoon]

description: 1. Give the child two plastic shaker eggs. 2. Put on rhythmic marching music. 3. Encourage the child to shake the eggs to the beat while marching around the room.
activity_photo: [Image: Child shaking eggs and marching]

description: 1. Provide a lightweight silk or chiffon scarf. 2. Play classical or instrumental music. 3. Show the child how to wave the scarf high and low, following the tempo of the music.
activity_photo: [Image: Child waving a scarf while dancing]

description: 1. Place a toddler-safe xylophone on the floor. 2. Show the child how to use the mallet to strike the keys from largest to smallest. 3. Encourage them to strike hard for loud sounds and soft for quiet sounds.
activity_photo: [Image: Child tapping a xylophone key]

description: 1. Set out wooden blocks with large carved or painted letters. 2. Point to the first letter of the child's name (e.g., 'A'). 3. Help the child trace the shape of the letter with their finger while you say the letter sound.
toy_photo: [Image: Wooden block showing the letter A]
activity_photo: [Image: Child tracing a letter on a block]

description: 1. Open a board book with single, large illustrations per page. 2. Point clearly to the object and name it (e.g., 'Apple'). 3. Take the child's index finger and gently help them point to the same picture.
toy_photo: [Image: Open book with a single apple drawing]
activity_photo: [Image: Parent guiding infant's finger to point]

description: 1. Write the child's name in large, bold letters on a piece of cardboard. 2. Tape it to their bedroom door or play area. 3. Periodically point to it and say, 'Look, that says your name!', encouraging them to recognize the shape of the word.
activity_photo: [Image: Child looking at their name on a door]

description: 1. Gather a collection of items that have distinct large and small versions (e.g., large balls and small balls). 2. Create two zones: a 'Big' hoop and a 'Small' hoop. 3. Help the child sort the items into the correct size category.
activity_photo: [Image: Child putting a small ball in a sorting ring]

description: 1. Line up exactly three small toys on a table. 2. Take the child's hand and have them point to each toy one at a time. 3. Say the numbers 'One, Two, Three' out loud only when their finger touches the object.
toy_photo: [Image: Three toy cars in a row]
activity_photo: [Image: Child touching one car at a time]

description: 1. Draw the outline of a triangle, square, and circle on a large paper. 2. Give the child physical blocks of those exact shapes. 3. Ask them to place the blocks inside the matching outlines on the paper.
toy_photo: [Image: Shape blocks next to drawn outlines]
activity_photo: [Image: Child placing a square block on a drawn square]

description: 1. Place two plates on the table. Put one cracker on the left plate and five on the right plate. 2. Ask the child, 'Which one has MORE?'. 3. Encourage them to point to the plate with the larger quantity, building spatial math logic.
toy_photo: [Image: Two plates with uneven amounts of crackers]
activity_photo: [Image: Child pointing to the plate with more snacks]

description: 1. Go outside to a safe concrete area. 2. Give the child a thick, jumbo piece of sidewalk chalk. 3. Encourage them to use whole-arm movements to make broad strokes and scribbles on the ground.
activity_photo: [Image: Child drawing on concrete with chalk]

description: 1. Stick multiple strips of colorful painter's tape to a flat surface, crossing them over each other. 2. Fold the ends over slightly to create tabs. 3. Encourage the child to use a pincer grasp to peel the tape off one by one.
toy_photo: [Image: Criss-crossed painter's tape on a tray]
activity_photo: [Image: Child pinching and pulling tape off a table]

description: 1. Stick a lump of playdough on the table and plant a dry spaghetti noodle vertically into it. 2. Give the child a bowl of penne or rigatoni pasta. 3. Show them how to carefully drop the pasta tubes over the upright noodle.
toy_photo: [Image: Dry pasta tubes and spaghetti sticks]
activity_photo: [Image: Child threading pasta onto a stick]

description: 1. Find a medium-sized cardboard box and place a few heavy books inside for resistance. 2. Place it on a smooth floor. 3. Encourage the child to place their hands on the box and use their leg strength to push it across the room.
activity_photo: [Image: Child leaning forward to push a box]

description: 1. Lay out several rubber mats or thin pillows across the floor with small gaps between them. 2. Tell the child the floor is 'water' and they must stay on the 'stones'. 3. Encourage them to step carefully from one marker to the next.
activity_photo: [Image: Child balancing while stepping on a marker]

description: 1. Stand the child on a very low, sturdy step (like a solid book or a 2-inch step stool). 2. Hold both of their hands securely. 3. Count '1, 2, 3!' and encourage them to jump forward with both feet landing at the same time.
activity_photo: [Image: Child jumping off a small step while holding hands]

description: 1. Fill a small bin with dry rice or beans. 2. Hide three small, distinctly shaped toys (e.g., a car, a block, a plastic animal) under the surface. 3. Ask the child to dig in and find all three, encouraging object permanence.
tools: Bin of dry rice, three small toys
toy_photo: [Image: Bin filled with rice covering small objects]
activity_photo: [Image: Child digging through rice to find a toy]

description: 1. Take out 3 plastic food containers of vastly different shapes (e.g., square, small circle, large rectangle) and their lids. 2. Mix the lids up. 3. Ask the child to figure out which lid snaps onto which container based on shape and size.
tools: Three mismatched plastic containers and lids
activity_photo: [Image: Child trying to press a lid onto a container]

description: 1. Tape an empty paper towel tube vertically to a wall or the leg of a table. 2. Place a basket at the bottom. 3. Give the child a small ball (that fits the tube) and let them drop it in the top and watch it fall into the basket.
toy_photo: [Image: Cardboard tube and a small ball]
activity_photo: [Image: Child dropping a ball into a tube on the wall]

description: 1. Tie a string or ribbon to a favorite toy. 2. Place the toy just out of the infant's reach, but lay the string near their hand. 3. Encourage them to pull the string toward themselves to retrieve the toy, teaching cause and effect.
toy_photo: [Image: Toy car with a string attached]
activity_photo: [Image: Infant pulling a string to get a toy]

description: 1. Provide a toddler-safe lock and key toy set. 2. Show the child how the key goes into the slot and turns. 3. Let them experiment with rotating the key to make the lock pop open.
activity_photo: [Image: Child turning a key in a toy lock]

description: 1. Sit in front of a mirror with the child. 2. Ask, 'Can you show me a sad face?' and mimic pouting. 3. Next, ask for a 'surprised face' and open your eyes wide, helping the child connect facial expressions to feelings.
activity_photo: [Image: Child making a surprised face in the mirror]

description: 1. Sit in a small circle with the child and another family member or a large teddy bear. 2. Say, 'I pass the ball to [Child's Name]'. 3. Prompt the child to pass the ball to the next person, teaching basic turn-taking.
activity_photo: [Image: Child handing a ball to another person]

description: 1. Make a crying sound and point to a baby doll. 2. Say, 'Oh no, the baby is sad. Can you help her?'. 3. Encourage the child to pat the doll's back, sing a song, or offer a blanket to build empathy.
activity_photo: [Image: Child hugging and patting a doll]

description: 1. Set up a single toy ramp or slide. 2. Take a toy car and say, 'My turn,' then roll it down. 3. Hand it to the child and say, 'Your turn,' enforcing the waiting period while someone else uses a shared resource.
activity_photo: [Image: Child waiting their turn to roll a car]

description: 1. Have an older sibling or another adult sit with the infant. 2. Have the second person hide behind a towel and pop out. 3. Watch the infant engage socially and laugh, bonding with individuals other than the primary caregiver.
activity_photo: [Image: Sibling playing peek-a-boo with baby]

description: 1. After a messy meal, dampen a washcloth. 2. Hand it to the child and point to your own mouth. 3. Encourage them to wipe their own mouth and chin before you step in to help finish the job.
activity_photo: [Image: Child clumsily wiping their face with a cloth]

description: 1. Hold up a loose-fitting jacket or button-down shirt. 2. Guide the child's right arm into the sleeve opening. 3. Encourage them to push their arm all the way through until their hand pops out the other side.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pushing arm through a jacket sleeve]

description: 1. Once the child's feet are through the pant legs, have them stand up. 2. Tell them to grab the waistband on both sides. 3. Encourage them to pull the pants up to their waist independently.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pulling up their own pants]

description: 1. Place a few dry crackers on a plastic, non-breakable plate. 2. Ask the child to hold the plate with two hands. 3. Have them walk slowly from the kitchen counter to their eating table without dropping the food.
activity_photo: [Image: Child carefully carrying a plate to a table]

description: 1. Give the child a soft-bristled baby brush. 2. Look in a mirror together. 3. Let the child attempt to drag the brush over their own head, praising their effort to participate in personal grooming.
activity_photo: [Image: Child trying to brush their own hair]

description: 1. Place a few heavy towels in a plastic laundry basket on a carpeted floor. 2. Tell the child to act like a bulldozer. 3. Have them lean against the basket and push it, engaging their core and joint receptors.
toy_photo: [Image: Plastic laundry basket filled with clothes]
activity_photo: [Image: Child pushing a heavy basket across a room]

description: 1. Call out an animal that requires heavy joint compression. 2. Ask them to 'Walk like a bear' (hands and feet flat on the floor, hips high). 3. Then try 'Walk like a crab' (sitting, hands behind, lifting bottom off the floor).
toy_photo: [Image: Illustrations of a bear and a crab]
activity_photo: [Image: Child demonstrating a bear crawl]

description: 1. Pile several soft, thick cushions or bean bags on the floor. 2. Have the child stand on a safe, soft surface nearby. 3. Count '1, 2, 3, CRASH!' and let them flop safely into the pile to receive deep pressure input.
tools: Bean bags or thick sofa cushions
activity_photo: [Image: Child laughing while falling into a pile of pillows]

description: 1. Tape a piece of contact paper to the wall with the sticky side facing out. 2. Give the child lightweight plastic balls or crumpled paper. 3. Have them throw or press the items onto the sticky surface so they hang there.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pressing a ball onto a sticky wall]

description: 1. Blow up a balloon and hang it from the ceiling with a string so it rests at the child's chest height. 2. Give the child a clean fly swatter or lightweight rolled-up magazine. 3. Encourage them to swing and hit the balloon.
activity_photo: [Image: Child batting at a hanging balloon]

description: 1. Dim the lights and give the child a flashlight. Turn one on for yourself. 2. Move your light beam across the wall. 3. Ask the child to use their light beam to 'catch' or overlap your light beam.
activity_photo: [Image: Two flashlight beams overlapping on a wall]

description: 1. Provide two small pitchers. Fill one halfway with dry kidney beans or chickpeas. 2. Set them on a tray to catch spills. 3. Show the child how to hold the handle and pour the beans from one pitcher to the other.
tools: Two small pitchers, dry beans, tray
activity_photo: [Image: Child pouring beans between pitchers]

description: 1. Go outside to a dry concrete patio or sidewalk. 2. Give the child a bucket of plain water and a large, clean paintbrush. 3. Let them 'paint' the concrete, watching the color change and then evaporate.
activity_photo: [Image: Child painting water on a sidewalk]

description: 1. Stick small pieces of hook-and-loop fastener (Velcro) to wooden blocks. 2. Press them firmly onto a felt board or carpet. 3. Encourage the infant to use their hands to grip and pull the blocks off with force.
toy_photo: [Image: Wooden block with a velcro strip]
activity_photo: [Image: Infant pulling a block off a felt board]

description: 1. Fill a clear plastic bottle with water, oil, and glitter. Seal the cap tightly. 2. Lay the child on their tummy. 3. Roll the bottle just out of reach so they can watch the glitter swirl and reach for the shiny object.
activity_photo: [Image: Infant reaching for a rolling sensory bottle]

description: 1. Place small toys inside the cups of a muffin tin. 2. Use painter's tape to tape over the top of each cup, trapping the toy. 3. Challenge the child to figure out how to peel or break the tape to rescue the toys.
tools: Muffin tin, painter's tape, small toys
toy_photo: [Image: Muffin tin covered in strips of tape]
activity_photo: [Image: Child peeling tape off a tin to get a toy]

description: 1. Freeze small plastic toys (like dinosaurs) inside a block of ice using a Tupperware container. 2. Place the ice block in a basin. 3. Give the child a dropper and warm water to melt the ice and 'rescue' the toys.
tools: Frozen ice block with toys, warm water, dropper
activity_photo: [Image: Child using a water dropper on ice]

description: 1. Take a jacket with a large, chunky zipper. 2. Connect the zipper at the bottom for the child. 3. Encourage them to pinch the zipper pull and drag it all the way up to the top.
toy_photo: [Image: Close up of a large plastic zipper]
activity_photo: [Image: Child pulling a zipper up a jacket]

description: 1. Give the child a colorful, corrugated plastic pop tube. 2. Show them how to hold one end in each hand. 3. Encourage them to pull their hands apart to stretch the tube, then push them together to collapse it, listening to the sound.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pulling a pop tube apart with both hands]

description: 1. Lay the infant on their back. 2. Hold a visually engaging toy over their right shoulder. 3. Guide their left hand across their body to reach for and grab the toy, then switch sides.
activity_photo: [Image: Infant reaching across their chest for a toy]

description: 1. Sit the child on a partially inflated exercise or therapy ball. 2. Hold them securely at the hips. 3. Gently bounce the ball up and down, encouraging the child to engage their stomach muscles to stay upright.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent holding a toddler bouncing on a ball]

description: 1. Play a fast, upbeat song and encourage the child to dance wildly. 2. Randomly pause the music. 3. Shout 'Freeze!' and encourage the child to stop moving instantly until the music resumes.
activity_photo: [Image: Child frozen in a funny dance pose]

description: 1. Cut a small wedge of fresh lemon. 2. Let the child touch their tongue to the lemon. 3. Narrate their reaction by saying 'Wow, that is sour!' to help them identify strong flavor profiles.
activity_photo: [Image: Child making a sour face after tasting lemon]

description: 1. Hold a colorful plastic pinwheel in front of the child's face. 2. Instruct them to take a big breath in through their nose. 3. Have them blow out through their mouth to make the pinwheel spin rapidly.
activity_photo: [Image: Child blowing forcefully on a pinwheel]

description: 1. Place small, dry items (like pom-poms or blocks) inside a kitchen salad spinner. 2. Place the lid on top. 3. Show the child how to push the top button or turn the crank to make the items blur together in a spin.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pressing the button on a salad spinner]

description: 1. Provide a sterilized, textured silicone chewy tube. 2. Place the tube near the infant's molars (side of the mouth). 3. Encourage them to bite down to provide proprioceptive feedback to their jaw joints.
activity_photo: [Image: Infant biting down on a textured silicone toy]
