activity_photo: [Image: Child pulling a matching shoe from a pile]

description: 1. Place three identical items (like three spoons) and one completely different item (like a toy car) in a row. 2. Ask, 'Which one doesn't belong?' 3. Help them identify the outlier.
tools: Three identical items, one different item
toy_photo: [Image: Three spoons and a toy car]
activity_photo: [Image: Child pointing to the toy car]

description: 1. During laundry time, set out a white shirt and a black shirt. 2. Give the child a pile of clothes. 3. Ask them to put the 'light' clothes with the white shirt and the 'dark' clothes with the black shirt.
activity_photo: [Image: Child sorting a black sock into the dark pile]

description: 1. Place a tennis ball, a softball, and a large beach ball on the floor. 2. Say, 'Bring me the BIGGEST ball.' 3. They must compare the objects visually to determine relative size.
toy_photo: [Image: Tennis ball, soft ball, beach ball]
activity_photo: [Image: Child hugging the large beach ball]

description: 1. Take a large broom and start sweeping the kitchen floor. 2. Give the child a small toy broom or a dry mop. 3. Let them sweep alongside you, copying your domestic actions.
activity_photo: [Image: Child sweeping next to parent]

description: 1. Give the child a spare, dry toothbrush and a plastic doll or dinosaur. 2. Mimic brushing your own teeth. 3. Encourage the child to brush the toy's teeth, practicing self-care routines through play.
activity_photo: [Image: Child brushing a toy dinosaur's teeth]

description: 1. At mealtime, hold up your cup. 2. Say 'Cheers!' enthusiastically and gently clink your cup against the child's cup. 3. Encourage them to initiate the 'cheers' ritual at the next meal.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent and child clinking cups]

description: 1. When water spills on the table, grab a cloth and wipe it up. 2. Hand the child the cloth. 3. Say, 'Can you help wipe?' and let them mimic the cleaning motion.
activity_photo: [Image: Child wiping a table with a cloth]

activity: Putting a Hat on a Bear
description: 1. Put a winter hat on your own head. 2. Give the child a hat and a teddy bear. 3. Encourage the child to dress the bear just like you dressed yourself.
activity_photo: [Image: Child stretching a hat over a bear's head]

description: 1. Take a wooden block, hold it to your ear, and have a fake, animated conversation. 2. Hand the block to the child. 3. Say, 'It's for you!' and watch them mimic the social behavior of talking on the phone.
activity_photo: [Image: Child babbling into a wooden block]

description: 1. Show the child how you rock a real baby or sway back and forth. 2. Hand them a baby doll. 3. Whisper 'Shh, the baby is sleeping' and encourage them to sway and soothe the doll.
activity_photo: [Image: Child gently rocking a doll in their arms]

description: 1. Set a stuffed dog on the couch. 2. Give the child a familiar board book. 3. Suggest they 'Read a story to the doggy,' copying the way you read to them by pointing at pictures and babbling.
toy_photo: [Image: Open book and a stuffed dog]
activity_photo: [Image: Child showing a book's pages to a stuffed animal]

description: 1. While you are cooking, give the child a clean, empty pot and a wooden spoon. 2. Let them stand in a safe area and 'stir the soup' just like you are doing.
toy_photo: [Image: Small metal pot and wooden spoon]
activity_photo: [Image: Child stirring vigorously in an empty pot]

description: 1. Hold your hand out in a fist. 2. Say 'Fist bump!' and gently tap the child's hand. 3. Encourage them to make a fist and initiate the social greeting with other family members.
activity_photo: [Image: Child giving an adult a fist bump]

description: 1. Fill a shallow tray with dry rolled oats. 2. Bury a few small plastic toys in the oats. 3. Encourage the child to plunge their hands into the dusty, flaky texture to find the toys.
activity_photo: [Image: Child digging hands into dry oatmeal]

description: 1. Boil a handful of spaghetti noodles, rinse them in cold water, and let them cool completely. 2. Place them in a bowl. 3. Let the child touch, squish, and pull the cold, slimy noodles.
activity_photo: [Image: Child hesitantly touching wet noodles]

description: 1. Spray a dollop of unscented shaving cream on a child-safe mirror or sliding glass door. 2. Have the child use both hands to smear the fluffy foam all over the glass, experiencing the light, airy texture.
activity_photo: [Image: Child smearing foam on a glass door]

description: 1. Take the child to a clean sandbox or the beach. 2. Take off their shoes and socks. 3. Let them stand, walk, and wiggle their toes in the dry, gritty sand to desensitize the bottoms of their feet.
activity_photo: [Image: Child wiggling bare toes in the sand]

description: 1. Turn on a vibrating infant massage toy or a vibrating teether. 2. Gently touch it to the infant's back, then their arms, then let them hold it. 3. The intense mechanical vibration provides strong tactile input.
activity_photo: [Image: Infant holding a buzzing toy]

description: 1. Fill a bowl with cold water and add a few ice cubes. 2. Toss in some floating plastic toys. 3. Have the child reach their hands into the freezing water to retrieve the toys, experiencing extreme temperature safely.
activity_photo: [Image: Child reaching into ice water to get a toy]

description: 1. Create a 'feel box' with swatches of velvet, burlap, silk, and corduroy. 2. Take the child's hand and gently rub it against each fabric. 3. Narrate the feelings: 'This is scratchy. This is smooth.'
activity_photo: [Image: Infant feeling a piece of rough burlap]

description: 1. Place a few dollops of plain or food-colored yogurt on a highchair tray. 2. Strip the child to their diaper. 3. Encourage them to slap, smear, and taste the cold, wet yogurt like finger paint.
activity_photo: [Image: Child covered in yogurt painting on a tray]

description: 1. Tear off a fresh sheet on a clothing lint roller. 2. Lightly roll it over the child's arms or let them touch the sticky paper with their fingers. 3. The mild 'tacky' feeling is a unique sensory input.
activity_photo: [Image: Child touching the sticky side of a lint roller]

description: 1. Take a large, soft craft feather. 2. Gently and slowly drag the tip of the feather across the infant's cheeks, arms, and bottoms of their feet. 3. The incredibly light touch can elicit giggles and build sensory tolerance.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent tickling baby's foot with a feather]

description: 1. Take the child to a park with mature trees. 2. Place their hands directly on the rough tree trunk. 3. Say, 'Feel the bark, it's bumpy and rough!' connecting them with the natural environment.
activity_photo: [Image: Child rubbing their hands on a tree trunk]

description: 1. Go for a walk near a riverbed or garden. 2. Give the child a small bucket. 3. Encourage them to search for and pick up small, smooth stones, practicing visual scanning and fine motor grasp outdoors.
activity_photo: [Image: Child picking up a rock on a trail]

description: 1. Find a large, safe, fragrant flower (like a rose or dandelion). 2. Show the child how to lean in close. 3. Instruct them to take a big sniff through their nose to smell the natural scent.
activity_photo: [Image: Child leaning in to sniff a flower]

description: 1. Find an ant trail on the sidewalk. 2. Crouch down low with the child. 3. Encourage them to be very still and quiet, practicing patience and focused observation of tiny wildlife.
activity_photo: [Image: Child crouching to look at bugs on the sidewalk]

description: 1. After a rainstorm, dress the child in rain boots. 2. Find a shallow, safe puddle on a clean sidewalk. 3. Encourage them to jump with both feet to make a massive splash, experiencing cause and effect outdoors.
activity_photo: [Image: Child jumping in a muddy puddle]

description: 1. In autumn, gather several large, dry, brown leaves. 2. Have the child hold a leaf in both hands. 3. Tell them to squeeze their hands tightly together to crumble the leaf into tiny pieces.
activity_photo: [Image: Child crushing a dry leaf in their hands]

description: 1. Early in the morning, find a patch of clean grass covered in dew. 2. Strip the infant's feet bare. 3. Hold them securely and let the bottoms of their feet brush against the cool, wet grass blades.
toy_photo: [Image: Blades of grass with water drops]
activity_photo: [Image: Parent holding infant so their toes touch wet grass]

description: 1. Sit quietly outside or look out a large window. 2. When a bird flies by, point to it excitedly and say, 'Look, a bird!' 3. Encourage the child to track the bird visually across the sky and point to it.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pointing up at the sky]

description: 1. Provide a small hand trowel. 2. Designate a safe patch of soil in the garden. 3. Let the child dig, turn over the dark earth, and look for roots or worms (supervise closely to prevent eating dirt).
activity_photo: [Image: Child digging in dark garden dirt]

description: 1. Go to an area with pine trees. 2. Give the child a basket. 3. Have them pick up fallen pinecones, exploring the prickly texture and sorting them into the basket.
activity_photo: [Image: Child placing a pinecone into a basket]

activity: Reaching a Toy with a Stick
description: 1. Place a highly desired toy under a sofa where the child's arm cannot reach it. 2. Lay a cardboard tube or long toy stick nearby. 3. Wait to see if the child uses the stick as a tool to drag the toy out.
activity_photo: [Image: Child using a stick to reach under a couch]

description: 1. Place a block inside a tall, narrow plastic cup where the child's hand won't fit. 2. Give the cup to the child. 3. They must figure out that they need to turn the cup completely upside down to get the block.
activity_photo: [Image: Child turning a cup over to dump a block]

description: 1. Place a snack on a counter just out of the child's reach. 2. Place a sturdy step stool across the room. 3. Encourage them to figure out how to push the stool over to the counter to gain the height they need.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pushing a step stool toward a counter]

description: 1. Place a small toy inside a box that closes with a simple hook or sliding latch. 2. Hand the box to the child. 3. Let them manipulate the hardware through trial and error to unlock the lid.
toy_photo: [Image: Wooden box with a metal latch]
activity_photo: [Image: Child concentrating on opening a latch]

description: 1. Tape a picture high up on the wall. 2. Give the child three sturdy, flat cardboard boxes. 3. Ask them to build 'stairs' so a toy figure can reach the picture, requiring spatial reasoning.
activity_photo: [Image: Child stacking boxes to make stairs]

description: 1. Give the child a toy padlock and a ring with three distinct keys. 2. Only one key fits the lock. 3. Have the child test each key sequentially until they figure out which one works.
activity_photo: [Image: Child trying different keys in a lock]

description: 1. Lay out three strings on the floor. Only one is tied to a toy car, the others are loose. 2. Hand the ends of all three strings to the child. 3. Let them tug them to discover which string controls the car.
toy_photo: [Image: Toy car attached to one of three strings]
activity_photo: [Image: Child pulling strings to see which moves a car]

description: 1. Wrap a familiar toy completely in aluminum foil or tissue paper. 2. Hand the shiny ball to the child. 3. They must problem-solve how to tear, peel, and pull the layers apart to access the object inside.
activity_photo: [Image: Child tearing foil off a hidden toy]

description: 1. Put a few crackers inside a small, zippered makeup pouch. 2. Give the pouch to the child. 3. They must hold the bag with one hand and figure out how to pull the zipper tab with the other to get the food.
activity_photo: [Image: Child struggling to pull a zipper open]

activity: Pushing a Block Out of a Tube
description: 1. Wedge a small, soft block halfway into a paper towel tube. 2. Give the child the tube and a wooden spoon handle. 3. The child must deduce that they need to insert the spoon into the other end to poke the block out.
toy_photo: [Image: Tube with a block stuck inside]
activity_photo: [Image: Child using a spoon handle to poke a block out of a tube]

description: 1. Provide a plastic cup and a small block. 2. Ask the child to put the block 'IN' the cup. 3. Empty it, then ask them to put the block 'UNDER' the cup, teaching basic prepositions through action.
toy_photo: [Image: Plastic cup and a wooden block]
activity_photo: [Image: Child placing a block under a plastic cup]

description: 1. Stand two large sofa pillows upright on the floor with a narrow gap between them. 2. Place a toy on the other side. 3. Encourage the child to turn their body sideways to squeeze 'BETWEEN' the pillows.
activity_photo: [Image: Child squeezing sideways between two cushions]

description: 1. Have the child stand facing away from a laundry basket. 2. Give them a soft ball. 3. Ask them to reach over their head or over their shoulder to throw the ball 'BEHIND' them into the basket.
activity_photo: [Image: Child tossing a ball backward over their shoulder]

description: 1. Place a small chair in the center of the room. 2. Tell the child, 'Stand NEXT TO the chair.' 3. Practice other directions like 'Stand BEHIND the chair' or 'Stand IN FRONT OF the chair.'
activity_photo: [Image: Child standing proudly beside a small chair]

description: 1. Hold a brightly colored toy up high near the ceiling and say 'UP!' 2. Wait for the infant to look up and reach. 3. Quickly bring the toy down to the floor and say 'DOWN!' so they adjust their gaze and posture.
activity_photo: [Image: Infant looking up at a toy held high]

description: 1. Provide a set of 5 nesting cups scattered on the floor. 2. Show the child that a big cup cannot fit inside a small cup. 3. Have them practice placing the cups inside one another in the correct spatial order.
activity_photo: [Image: Child fitting a smaller cup into a larger one]

description: 1. Stand with your legs spread wide apart like a bridge. 2. Hold a toy behind you. 3. Call the child to crawl 'THROUGH' your legs to get to the toy, judging the size of their body against the opening.
activity_photo: [Image: Child crawling through parent's open legs]

description: 1. Point to a low bookshelf with two open shelves. 2. Give the child two books. 3. Ask them to put one book on the 'TOP' shelf and the other book on the 'BOTTOM' shelf.
activity_photo: [Image: Child placing a book on a bottom shelf]

description: 1. Cut a round hole in the center of a piece of cardboard. 2. Give the child a wooden spoon or a thick marker. 3. Have them hold the cardboard and guide the stick 'THROUGH' the hole.
tools: Cardboard with a hole, wooden spoon
toy_photo: [Image: Cardboard square with a center hole]
activity_photo: [Image: Child pushing a spoon handle through a hole in cardboard]

description: 1. Lay a long body pillow flat on the floor. 2. Sit the infant on one side and sit yourself on the other. 3. Encourage them to climb 'OVER' the obstacle to reach you.
activity_photo: [Image: Infant climbing over a long pillow]

description: 1. Place a 1-minute visual sand timer on the table. 2. Tell the child, 'Let's watch the sand fall until it's all gone.' 3. Practice sitting quietly and maintaining focus on the moving sand for the full minute.
activity_photo: [Image: Child staring intently at a sand timer]

description: 1. Give the child a full sheet of construction paper. 2. Show them how to rip it into small strips. 3. Encourage them to keep ripping until the entire piece of paper is completely shredded, building task persistence.
activity_photo: [Image: Child tearing paper into many small pieces]

description: 1. Give the child six large building blocks. 2. Ask them to build the tallest tower they can. 3. Praise them for staying focused on balancing the blocks until all six are used.
activity_photo: [Image: Child carefully placing a sixth block on a tower]

description: 1. Place exactly ten counting bears in a bowl. 2. Set out an empty cup. 3. Have the child transfer all ten bears into the cup one by one, keeping their attention on the task until the bowl is empty.
activity_photo: [Image: Child moving the last bear into a cup]

description: 1. Wind up a music box that plays a tune for about 30 seconds. 2. Set it on the floor. 3. Sit quietly with the infant, encouraging them to listen and watch the box until the music stops completely.
activity_photo: [Image: Infant listening quietly to a music box]

description: 1. Provide a wooden puzzle with exactly three large, distinct pieces. 2. Remove all the pieces. 3. Sit with the child and offer light guidance to keep them focused until all three pieces are back in their spots.
toy_photo: [Image: Wooden puzzle with three animal shapes]
activity_photo: [Image: Child fitting the final piece into a puzzle]

description: 1. Sit facing the child with legs in a V-shape. 2. Roll a ball to them and count 'One!'. 3. Encourage them to stay engaged in the back-and-forth game until you reach 'Ten!'.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent and child rolling a ball back and forth]

description: 1. Hide five bright stickers around a small room at the child's eye level. 2. Tell them they need to find all five. 3. Encourage them to keep looking and not give up until the final sticker is found.
activity_photo: [Image: Child searching for a sticker under a chair]

description: 1. Draw a medium-sized circle on a piece of paper. 2. Give the child a crayon. 3. Ask them to color inside the circle and gently encourage them to keep going until the whole shape is filled with color.
activity_photo: [Image: Child scribbling intently inside a circle]

description: 1. Set up a simple cardboard ramp. 2. Roll a toy car down the ramp three times in a row. 3. Watch to see if the infant maintains visual focus on the car for the duration of the repeated action.
activity_photo: [Image: Infant tracking a car rolling down a ramp]

description: 1. Show the child a small snack. 2. Hide it in one of your closed fists behind your back, then bring both fists forward. 3. Ask the child to tap the hand that is hiding the treat.
tools: Small snack (e.g., a puff or raisin)
activity_photo: [Image: Child tapping parent's closed fist]

description: 1. While in the living room, give a two-step verbal instruction. 2. Say, 'Go to the kitchen and bring me a spoon.' 3. The child must hold both the location and the object in their mind to complete the task.
activity_photo: [Image: Child returning from another room holding a spoon]

description: 1. Show a toy cow and say 'Moo!' 2. Hide the cow behind your back and talk about something else for 5 seconds. 3. Bring the cow back out and ask, 'What does the cow say?' to test brief recall.
activity_photo: [Image: Child looking at a toy cow]

description: 1. Look at the child and say a silly two-word phrase, like 'Blue Banana!' 2. Wait 3 seconds. 3. Ask them to repeat the exact phrase back to you.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent and child exchanging words]

description: 1. Show the child a red sock and place it under a cup. 2. Show them a blue sock and place it under a different cup. 3. Hand them a second red sock and ask, 'Which cup has the matching sock?'
tools: Two pairs of distinct socks, two cups
toy_photo: [Image: Red and blue socks with two cups]
activity_photo: [Image: Child lifting a cup to find a matching sock]

description: 1. Sit facing the child. 2. Tap your knees three times in a specific rhythm (e.g., tap-tap, pause, tap). 3. Ask the child to hold that rhythm in their mind and repeat it back to you exactly.
activity_photo: [Image: Child tapping their knees in a pattern]

description: 1. Hold up a familiar item, like the child's toothbrush or a bath toy. 2. Ask, 'Where does this go?' 3. Have the child recall the spatial location of the object and walk to the bathroom to put it away.
activity_photo: [Image: Child carrying a toothbrush to the bathroom]

description: 1. Place two items (a ball and a block) on a tray. 2. Have the child close their eyes, and remove the ball. 3. When they open their eyes, ask them to recall which item is missing from the original set.
toy_photo: [Image: Tray with a block and empty space]
activity_photo: [Image: Child looking confused at an empty spot on a tray]

description: 1. Show the infant a toy, then place it under a blanket while they watch. 2. Distract them for 2-3 seconds by calling their name. 3. See if they remember to turn back and pull the blanket off the toy.
activity_photo: [Image: Infant pulling a blanket off to find a toy]

description: 1. Draw a very simple 'map' (e.g., an arrow pointing to a drawing of a couch). 2. Hide a sticker on the couch. 3. Show the child the map and have them hold that information in their mind to find the sticker.
activity_photo: [Image: Child holding a paper map looking at a couch]

description: 1. When outside and you hear an airplane, point to the sky. 2. Say, 'Look, an airplane!' 3. Ensure the child follows your point, looks at the plane, and then looks back at your face to share the experience.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent and child looking up and pointing at the sky]

description: 1. Sit the infant in your lap with a board book. 2. Point to a picture of a dog and say 'Dog'. 3. Watch to see if the infant follows your finger to the picture, rather than just looking at your face.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent pointing to a book while infant watches]

description: 1. Blow bubbles toward the child. 2. Exaggerate popping a bubble with your finger and say 'Pop!' 3. Encourage the child to pop one and immediately look at you to share the fun.
activity_photo: [Image: Child popping a bubble and smiling at parent]

description: 1. Start building a block tower. 2. Hand a block to the child, gesturing for them to add it to the stack. 3. Alternate taking turns, sharing eye contact and smiles as the tower gets higher.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent and child taking turns stacking blocks]

activity: Looking at Parent After a Loud Noise
description: 1. When an unexpected noise happens (e.g., dropping a book), react with a mild, surprised face. 2. Wait to see if the infant looks at the dropped book, and then immediately looks at your face to gauge your reaction.
activity_photo: [Image: Infant looking from a dropped item to parent's face]

description: 1. Sit quietly across the room while the child plays. 2. Wait for the child to discover something interesting. 3. Praise them heavily if they pick up the item, walk over, and hold it up specifically to show it to you.
activity_photo: [Image: Child walking over to hand a parent a toy]

description: 1. Sit facing the infant. 2. Suddenly widen your eyes, turn your head prominently, and stare at a toy on the floor. 3. Do not point. See if the infant follows your line of sight to look at the same object.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent staring at a toy and infant following their gaze]

description: 1. Put on an upbeat song. 2. Hold both of the child's hands and bounce to the music. 3. Maintain eye contact and smile, fostering a shared experience of joy and rhythm.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent and child holding hands and dancing]

activity: Passing a Toy Back and Forth
description: 1. Hand a rattle to the infant. 2. Put your hand out and ask for it back. 3. Establish a cycle of giving and receiving, ensuring the infant makes eye contact during the exchange.
activity_photo: [Image: Infant handing a rattle back to parent]

description: 1. Put a fun toy inside a shoebox. 2. Shake it and say, 'I wonder what is inside?!' 3. Open it dramatically together. Ensure the child looks at the toy, then looks up at you to share the excitement.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent and child looking into an open box together]

description: 1. Place 3 or 4 large blocks in a line on the floor, spaced a foot apart. 2. Show the child how to step over each one without kicking it. 3. This requires them to plan their foot placement and lift their knees high.
activity_photo: [Image: Child stepping carefully over a block]

description: 1. Place an empty, sturdy laundry basket on a carpeted floor. 2. Throw a toy inside. 3. Encourage the child to figure out how to lift their leg high enough to climb inside the basket to get the toy.
activity_photo: [Image: Child throwing a leg over the edge of a basket]

description: 1. Identify a sturdy dining chair on a smooth floor. 2. Ask the child to help you move it to another spot. 3. They must plan how to position their hands and use their body weight to push the object.
activity_photo: [Image: Child leaning against a chair to push it]

description: 1. Stand facing the child. 2. Perform a sequence: Touch your nose, then clap your hands. 3. Ask the child to repeat the sequence exactly, requiring them to hold and execute a motor plan.
toy_photo: [Image: Icon of touching nose and clapping]
activity_photo: [Image: Child touching nose then clapping]

description: 1. Scatter pillows to create a winding path on the floor. 2. Tell the child the floor is hot lava. 3. Encourage them to jump or step from pillow to pillow, planning their route to the other side of the room.
activity_photo: [Image: Child jumping from one pillow to another]

description: 1. Give the child a toy on a string (like a pull-dog or a wagon). 2. Instruct them to pull it toward you. 3. To watch the toy while pulling it, they will naturally have to plan how to walk backward safely.
activity_photo: [Image: Child walking backward pulling a toy]

description: 1. Place a large, thick, sturdy book (like a dictionary) flat on the floor. 2. Hold the child's hand. 3. Ask them to step up onto the book with one foot, then the other, practicing a small elevation change.
activity_photo: [Image: Child stepping onto a thick book]

description: 1. Place a dining chair on the floor. 2. Sit on one side and call the crawling infant from the other side. 3. The infant must plan how to lower their body to navigate under the rungs of the chair.
activity_photo: [Image: Infant crawling under a dining chair]

description: 1. Lay out a soft yoga mat. 2. Instruct the child to lie down straight with their arms by their sides. 3. Tell them to roll like a hotdog from one end of the mat to the other, requiring whole-body coordination.
activity_photo: [Image: Child rolling sideways down a mat]

description: 1. Stand a few feet away from the child. 2. Slowly roll a large ball toward them. 3. The child must time their leg swing to intercept and kick the ball while it is in motion.
activity_photo: [Image: Child timing a kick as a ball rolls toward them]

activity: Passing a Block Left to Right
description: 1. Hand a small block to the infant's right hand. 2. Offer a second block to their right hand. 3. To take the new block, they must transfer the first block across their body to their left hand.
activity_photo: [Image: Infant transferring a block from one hand to the other]

activity: Wiping a Table with One Hand
description: 1. Give the child a damp cloth. 2. Have them place their left hand behind their back. 3. Instruct them to use their right hand to wipe the entire table, forcing them to sweep their arm across their midline.
activity_photo: [Image: Child wiping a table using large arm sweeps]

description: 1. Have the child sit at a table. 2. Place a small snack far over on their left side. 3. Gently hold their left hand down so they must reach their right arm across their chest to grab the food.
activity_photo: [Image: Child reaching across their body to grab a snack]

activity: Putting a Sticker on the Opposite Arm
description: 1. Give the child a sticker. 2. Have them hold it in their right hand. 3. Tell them to place the sticker on their left shoulder, requiring them to cross their arm over their body.
activity_photo: [Image: Child placing a sticker on their opposite shoulder]

description: 1. Place two toy drums (or pots) in front of the child, one on the far left and one on the far right. 2. Give them one mallet in their right hand. 3. Have them hit the right drum, then cross over to hit the left drum.
tools: Two drums or pots, one mallet
toy_photo: [Image: Two pots and a wooden spoon]
activity_photo: [Image: Child reaching across body to hit a drum]

activity: Twisting to Hand a Toy Behind
description: 1. Have the child sit on the floor. 2. Sit directly behind them. 3. Hand them a toy over their right shoulder. Ask them to twist to their left to hand the toy back to you.
activity_photo: [Image: Child twisting torso to hand a toy backward]

description: 1. Put a jacket on the child and zip it up halfway. 2. Show them how to hold the bottom of the jacket with one hand. 3. Instruct them to pinch the zipper tab with the other hand and pull down to unzip.
activity_photo: [Image: Child holding jacket bottom while unzipping]

description: 1. Give the child a thick, washable marker with the cap tightly on. 2. Show them how to hold the barrel with one hand and the cap with the other. 3. Have them pull their hands apart forcefully to pop the cap off.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pulling a cap off a marker]

activity: Holding a Cup with Two Hands
description: 1. Provide a small, open cup with a tiny amount of water. 2. Guide the infant to place one hand on each side of the cup. 3. Help them coordinate lifting the cup symmetrically to their mouth to drink.
activity_photo: [Image: Infant holding a cup with both hands to drink]

description: 1. Tie a toy to a long, thick rope. 2. Lay the toy far away. 3. Show the child how to grab the rope with one hand, pull, then reach forward with the *other* hand to pull again, bringing the toy closer.
toy_photo: [Image: Thick rope attached to a toy]
activity_photo: [Image: Child pulling a rope hand-over-hand]

description: 1. Blend a thick smoothie using yogurt and frozen fruit. 2. Provide a standard-sized straw. 3. The child must use strong lip seal and cheek suction to pull the heavy liquid up the straw.
toy_photo: [Image: Cup with a smoothie and straw]
activity_photo: [Image: Child sucking hard on a straw]

activity: Making Funny Faces in a Mirror
description: 1. Sit in front of a mirror with the child. 2. Puff your cheeks out with air, stick out your tongue, or pucker your lips like a fish. 3. Encourage the child to copy you to exercise their facial muscles.
activity_photo: [Image: Child making a fish face in a mirror]

description: 1. Close your lips tightly and hum a familiar tune like 'Twinkle Twinkle'. 2. Tell the child, 'Keep your lips closed tight and make a sound!' 3. Encourage them to hum along, teaching breath control and vocal cord use.
activity_photo: [Image: Child humming with lips pressed together]

description: 1. Offer a frozen fruit popsicle or a lollipop. 2. Instruct the child to stick their tongue out to lick it, rather than biting or sucking. 3. This builds tongue extension and mobility.
activity_photo: [Image: Child sticking tongue out to lick a popsicle]

description: 1. Hold up your index finger and pretend it's a lit candle. 2. Take a deep breath and blow forcefully at your finger. 3. Have the child try to 'blow out' your finger, practicing strong, directed exhalation.
toy_photo: [Image: Finger held up like a candle]
activity_photo: [Image: Child blowing hard at a parent's finger]

description: 1. Demonstrate making a 'cluck' or 'click' sound by suctioning your tongue to the roof of your mouth and dropping it. 2. Tell the child it sounds like horse hooves. 3. Encourage them to copy the complex tongue movement.
activity_photo: [Image: Child trying to make a clicking sound with their tongue]

description: 1. During bath time, take a small sip of water. 2. Puff your cheeks out and hold the water inside without swallowing or spitting. 3. Challenge the child to hold water in their cheeks for 3 seconds, building lip seal strength.
activity_photo: [Image: Child holding water in puffed cheeks]

description: 1. Provide a bowl of thick food (like oatmeal) and a toddler spoon. 2. Show the child how to scoop. 3. Let them feed themselves, accepting the mess as they practice the wrist rotation required to get the food to their mouth.
activity_photo: [Image: Child feeding themselves oatmeal with a spoon]

description: 1. Before bath time, loosen the heel of the child's sock. 2. Instruct them to grab the toe of the sock. 3. Encourage them to pull hard to remove the sock themselves.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pulling their own sock off]

description: 1. Ensure the child is wearing loose, elastic-waist pants. 2. During a diaper change or potty time, have them stand up. 3. Instruct them to put their thumbs inside the waistband and push down past their hips.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pushing their pants down by the waistband]

description: 1. Stand the child at the sink on a stool. 2. Put a drop of soap on their hands. 3. Instruct them to rub their palms together to make bubbles, then rinse the bubbles away under the water.
activity_photo: [Image: Child rubbing soapy hands together at a sink]

description: 1. Hand the child a damp washcloth after eating. 2. Tap your own chin and say 'Wipe your face.' 3. Encourage them to rub the cloth over their mouth to clean off food before you do the final wipe.
activity_photo: [Image: Child awkwardly wiping their face with a cloth]

description: 1. Bring an empty toy bin to the center of the room. 2. Hand a toy to the child and point to the bin. 3. Say 'Clean up!' and have them drop the toy in, establishing a routine for tidying.
activity_photo: [Image: Child dropping a toy block into a bin]

description: 1. Lay a small throw blanket flat on the floor. 2. Have the child hold two corners while you hold the other two. 3. Walk toward them and guide them to lay their corners down, creating a fold together.
activity_photo: [Image: Child holding corners of a blanket to fold it]

description: 1. Put a smear of toothpaste on a toddler brush. 2. Let the child hold the brush and 'scrub' their teeth first. 3. Afterward, take the brush and finish the job properly, ensuring they get a turn for independence.
activity_photo: [Image: Child attempting to brush their own teeth]

description: 1. Spray a mountain of shaving cream onto a tray. 2. Bury several plastic toys inside. 3. Have the child plunge their hands into the fluffy, wet foam to locate and pull out the hidden objects.
activity_photo: [Image: Child with foam-covered hands pulling a toy out]

description: 1. Tape a long sheet of bubble wrap to the floor. 2. Take off the child's shoes and socks. 3. Have them walk or stomp across the plastic, combining tactile foot stimulation with auditory 'pops'.
activity_photo: [Image: Child stepping barefoot on bubble wrap]

description: 1. Stick a thick strip of hook-and-loop fastener (Velcro) together. 2. Hand it to the infant. 3. Encourage them to pull the halves apart, experiencing the physical resistance and the loud ripping sound.
toy_photo: [Image: Strips of hook and loop fastener]
activity_photo: [Image: Infant ripping a velcro strip apart]

description: 1. Place two bowls on a towel: one filled with water, one empty. 2. Give the child a large sponge. 3. Have them soak the sponge, feel the heavy wetness, and squeeze it tightly over the empty bowl.
activity_photo: [Image: Child squeezing water out of a sponge]

description: 1. Rake a large pile of dry autumn leaves. 2. Have the child run and jump into the center. 3. This combines gross motor impact with the auditory crunch and the tactile feel of the brittle leaves.
activity_photo: [Image: Child jumping into a leaf pile]

description: 1. Lay a soft blanket flat on the floor. 2. Have the child lay down at one edge. 3. Hold the edge and gently lift it to roll the child up like a log, providing deep pressure and vestibular input.
activity_photo: [Image: Child giggling while being rolled in a blanket]

activity: Listening to a Metronome While Rocking
description: 1. Turn on a metronome app to a slow, steady heartbeat pace (60 BPM). 2. Hold the infant in your arms. 3. Rock them back and forth in perfect time with the auditory clicks to sync their senses.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent rocking infant rhythmically to a sound]

description: 1. Provide two small cups: one with cold fridge water, one with safely warm tap water. 2. Have the child take a tiny sip of the cold, then the warm. 3. Discuss the intense temperature contrast in their mouth.
tools: Two cups, warm and cold water
activity_photo: [Image: Child sipping cautiously from a cup]

description: 1. Cut a fresh orange in half. 2. Have the child touch the bumpy rind and the wet inside. 3. Bring it to their nose and encourage a deep sniff, combining tactile and olfactory exploration.
activity_photo: [Image: Child smelling a cut orange]

activity: Finding Heavy Objects in the Dark
description: 1. Place a heavy book and a light pillow in a dimly lit room. 2. Ask the child to go in and bring back the 'HEAVY' object. 3. They must rely on proprioceptive feedback (lifting) rather than sight.
toy_photo: [Image: Thick book and a small pillow]
activity_photo: [Image: Child lifting a heavy book in a dark room]

description: 1. Give a clear command: 'Pick up the ball and put it on the couch.' 2. Do not point or help. 3. Wait for the child to hold both instructions in their mind and execute them in order.
activity_photo: [Image: Child placing a ball onto a sofa]

description: 1. Hold up the child's left sneaker. 2. Say, 'Go find the other shoe that matches this.' 3. The child must remember the visual image of the shoe while walking to the closet to find it.
activity_photo: [Image: Child searching for a matching shoe]

activity: Pointing to a Named Body Part
description: 1. Sit facing the child. 2. Say quickly, 'Touch your ears!' 3. The child must retrieve the vocabulary word from memory and execute the physical action to point to the correct spot.
toy_photo: [Image: Icon of a face with prominent ears]
activity_photo: [Image: Child touching both of their ears]

activity: Putting a Toy Back Where It Belongs
description: 1. Hand the child a specific toy, like a puzzle piece. 2. Ask, 'Where does this live?' 3. The child must recall the spatial map of the room and return the item to its proper storage box or shelf.
activity_photo: [Image: Child walking to a shelf to put a toy away]

description: 1. Show the child a toy car. 2. Put it inside an opaque box and put the lid on. 3. Ask a random question like 'What color is your shirt?'. Then ask, 'What is inside the box?' to test delayed recall.
activity_photo: [Image: Child thinking before pointing to a box]

description: 1. Tape a large piece of paper to a wall or table. 2. Give the child a crayon in their dominant hand. 3. Instruct them to draw a continuous line from the far left side of the paper to the far right.
activity_photo: [Image: Child drawing a long line across a paper]

description: 1. Give the child a toddler-sized broom. 2. Show them how to hold it with both hands. 3. Have them sweep a pile of crumpled paper from one side of their body to the other, requiring trunk rotation.
activity_photo: [Image: Child sweeping paper across the floor]

activity: Touching Right Hand to Left Knee
description: 1. Sit facing the child. 2. Say, 'Take your right hand and touch your left knee!' while demonstrating. 3. Encourage them to copy the specific cross-body movement.
activity_photo: [Image: Child touching their opposite knee]

description: 1. Sit the child with a large board book on their lap. 2. Instruct them to keep their left hand still. 3. Ask them to use their right hand to reach across to the left page and flip it over to the right.
activity_photo: [Image: Child reaching across a book to turn a page]

description: 1. Stand a few feet away from the child. 2. Toss a large, lightweight ball gently toward their chest. 3. Instruct them to bring both arms together at the exact same time to trap the ball.
activity_photo: [Image: Child hugging a ball they just caught]

description: 1. Hand the child a small tub of playdough with the lid slightly loosened. 2. Show them how to hold the tub firmly with one hand. 3. Instruct them to use the other hand to pry the lid completely off.
activity_photo: [Image: Child struggling to pull a lid off a tub]

activity: Squeezing a Sponge in the Bath
description: 1. Give the child a large bath sponge. 2. Let it soak up water. 3. Instruct them to use both hands simultaneously to squeeze the sponge as hard as they can to get the water out.
activity_photo: [Image: Child squeezing a wet sponge with both hands]

description: 1. Hand the child a piece of construction paper. 2. Show them how to hold the top edge with both hands close together. 3. Instruct them to pull one hand forward and one hand backward to tear a strip.
activity_photo: [Image: Child's hands pulling paper in opposite directions]

description: 1. Provide a lump of dough and a child-sized rolling pin. 2. Have the child place one hand on each handle. 3. Instruct them to push away and pull back, applying even pressure from both arms to flatten the dough.
activity_photo: [Image: Child rolling out dough with two hands]

description: 1. Put on an upbeat, rhythmic song. 2. Sit facing the infant and clap your hands together loudly to the beat. 3. Encourage the infant to bring both of their hands together to join in the clapping.
activity_photo: [Image: Infant clapping hands while parent sings]

description: 1. Have the child hold three small plastic coins in the palm of their dominant hand. 2. Ask them to move one coin at a time to their fingertips. 3. Instruct them to drop the single coin into a piggy bank without dropping the others.
activity_photo: [Image: Child holding coins in palm while pinching one]

description: 1. Place several small beads or dry beans on a table. 2. Ask the child to pick them up one by one using their thumb and index finger. 3. Have them tuck each new piece into their palm and hold them all there while picking up more.
activity_photo: [Image: Child hiding picked-up beads inside their palm]

description: 1. Give the child a thick, unsharpened pencil. 2. Show them how to hold it like they are about to write. 3. Ask them to use only the fingers of that hand to flip the pencil over so the eraser points down.
activity_photo: [Image: Child using fingers to flip a pencil end-over-end]

description: 1. Provide a busy board or a toy radio with large, clicking dials. 2. Show the child how to grip the dial. 3. Instruct them to twist their fingers and wrist to turn the dial all the way to the right.
toy_photo: [Image: Plastic dial on a toy board]
activity_photo: [Image: Child rotating a toy dial with fingertips]

description: 1. Give the child a clean, empty baby nasal aspirator (bulb syringe) during bath time. 2. Show them how to hold it in one hand. 3. Have them squeeze the bulb with their whole palm to suck up and squirt water.
activity_photo: [Image: Child squeezing a rubber bulb in the bath]

description: 1. Hand the child a chunky wooden puzzle piece upside down. 2. Tell them to put it into the board. 3. They must use their fingers to rotate the piece 180 degrees within their hand before placing it.
activity_photo: [Image: Child turning a puzzle piece with their fingertips]

description: 1. Give the child a square of tissue paper. 2. Instruct them to hold it in one hand and put their other hand behind their back. 3. Have them use their fingers to crunch the paper up into a tiny, tight ball.
activity_photo: [Image: Child squeezing a paper ball with one hand]

description: 1. Provide a small, easy-to-spin wooden top. 2. Show the child how to grasp the stem with their thumb and pointer finger. 3. Demonstrate how to snap their fingers in opposite directions to make the top spin.
activity_photo: [Image: Child snapping fingers to spin a top]

activity: Opening a Padlock with a Key
description: 1. Provide a toddler-safe toy lock and key. 2. Once the key is inserted, the child must hold the lock steady with one hand. 3. They must use the fingertips of the other hand to turn the key until the lock pops.
activity_photo: [Image: Child turning a key with their fingertips]

description: 1. Take a clean, empty plastic water bottle with a wide lid. 2. Loosen the lid slightly. 3. Encourage the child to grip the lid and twist their wrist repeatedly to unscrew the cap entirely.
toy_photo: [Image: Plastic bottle with a wide cap]
activity_photo: [Image: Child twisting a cap off a bottle]

description: 1. Fill a clear plastic bottle with dry rice and three tiny distinct toys (e.g., a mini red car, a blue button). 2. Shake the bottle. 3. Ask the child to turn the bottle and visually locate the tiny car hidden in the rice.
tools: Clear bottle, dry rice, tiny toys
toy_photo: [Image: Bottle filled with rice and hidden trinkets]
activity_photo: [Image: Child turning a sensory bottle looking for a toy]

activity: Finding the Blue Block in a Bin
description: 1. Fill a storage bin with dozens of colorful plastic balls or mixed blocks. 2. Hide one specific blue block in the mix. 3. Tell the child to 'Find the blue square block' against the highly distracting visual background.
tools: Bin of mixed toys, one target block
toy_photo: [Image: Bin full of colorful mixed toys]
activity_photo: [Image: Child staring into a bin of toys searching]

activity: Spotting the Dog in a Busy Book
description: 1. Open a 'Look and Find' style book or a book with incredibly detailed, busy illustrations. 2. Point to a small dog in the background. 3. Ask the child, 'Can you find the little dog hiding by the tree?'
activity_photo: [Image: Child pointing to a tiny detail in a book]

description: 1. Place a chaotic pile of forks, spoons, and butter knives on the table. 2. Ask the child to extract ONLY the spoons. 3. They must visually separate the desired object shape from the overlapping visual clutter.
activity_photo: [Image: Child picking a spoon out of a messy pile]

activity: Finding a Coin on a Patterned Rug
description: 1. Lay down a rug or blanket with a loud, complex, colorful pattern. 2. Drop a large plastic coin on the rug. 3. Ask the child to find the coin, forcing their brain to separate the foreground object from the busy background.
toy_photo: [Image: Large coin on a floral rug]
activity_photo: [Image: Child scanning a rug for a coin]

description: 1. Give the child a sheet featuring 20 different animal stickers. 2. Say, 'Where is the monkey?' 3. The child must scan the entire visual field of similar objects to isolate the specific target.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pointing to a specific sticker on a full sheet]

activity: Finding the Red Crayon in a Box
description: 1. Open a large box of 24 or 48 mixed crayons. 2. Ask the child to pull out the red crayon. 3. They must visually filter out all the other colors and shapes to locate the exact one requested.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pulling a red crayon from a full box]

activity: Spotting a Toy in the Grass
description: 1. Toss a green or brown toy into the grass outside. 2. Ask the child to go find it. 3. The lack of strong color contrast forces them to rely on shape recognition to distinguish the toy from the grass.
activity_photo: [Image: Child searching through grass for a toy]

description: 1. Crumble a small cracker on a textured wooden table or speckled countertop. 2. Give the child a damp cloth. 3. Ask them to wipe up all the crumbs, requiring them to visually locate small items on a textured surface.
activity_photo: [Image: Child wiping small crumbs off a table]

activity: Finding Shoes in a Cluttered Closet
description: 1. Open a closet floor that is cluttered with bags, boots, and toys. 2. Say, 'Can you find your blue sneakers?' 3. The child must visually scan and mentally isolate their shoes from the surrounding mess.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pulling their shoes out of a messy pile]

description: 1. Place a round ball and a square block inside an opaque cloth bag. 2. Tell the child to reach in without looking. 3. Ask them to feel the shapes and pull out the 'round ball' based on touch alone.
activity_photo: [Image: Child reaching into a bag without looking]

description: 1. Bury a plastic spoon deep in a bin of dry rice. 2. Put a blindfold on the child or have them close their eyes. 3. Ask them to dig around until they feel the hard, long shape of the spoon and pull it out.
activity_photo: [Image: Child with closed eyes digging in rice]

description: 1. Provide two squares of sandpaper and two squares of silk. 2. Have the child close their eyes. 3. Hand them a piece of sandpaper and ask them to feel the remaining squares to find the matching rough texture.
activity_photo: [Image: Child feeling fabric squares with eyes closed]

description: 1. Have the child hold their hands behind their back. 2. Place a highly familiar object in their hands (like a toy car or a hairbrush). 3. Ask them to feel it and guess what it is without bringing it to the front to look.
activity_photo: [Image: Child feeling an object held behind their back]

activity: Finding the Keys in a Bag
description: 1. Drop a set of jingling metal keys into a large purse or tote bag filled with soft clothes. 2. Ask the child to reach in. 3. They must rely on tactile feedback (cold, hard metal) to locate and retrieve the keys.
activity_photo: [Image: Child rummaging in a purse to find keys]

description: 1. Fill a bowl with a mix of soft cotton balls and hard plastic coins. 2. Have the child close their eyes. 3. Ask them to use their hands to sift through the bowl and pull out only the hard coins.
toy_photo: [Image: Bowl mixed with cotton and coins]
activity_photo: [Image: Child sorting objects by feel with eyes closed]

activity: Is it Big or Small? (Touch Only)
description: 1. Place a very large ball and a tiny bouncy ball under a thick blanket. 2. Have the child slide their hands under the blanket. 3. Say, 'Bring me the BIG ball,' requiring them to gauge size purely by touch.
tools: Thick blanket, large ball, small ball
activity_photo: [Image: Child feeling under a blanket for objects]

description: 1. Hold a plastic fork and a plastic spoon behind your back. 2. Have the child reach around and feel both. 3. Ask them to grab the fork, requiring them to feel the prongs versus the smooth bowl of the spoon.
activity_photo: [Image: Child reaching behind parent's back to feel objects]

description: 1. Give the child a jacket while their eyes are closed. 2. Ask them to run their hands down the fabric. 3. Instruct them to stop when their fingers locate the metal/plastic zipper track.
toy_photo: [Image: Close up of a jacket zipper]
activity_photo: [Image: Child feeling a jacket blindly to find the zipper]

description: 1. Put a plastic cow and a plastic snake in a bag. 2. Ask the child to reach in. 3. Say, 'Can you feel the long, skinny snake? Pull it out!'
activity_photo: [Image: Child feeling inside a bag to identify a shape]

activity: Reaching While Standing on a Cushion
description: 1. Have the child stand on a squishy couch cushion on the floor. 2. Hold a toy slightly to their left or right side. 3. Encourage them to lean and reach for the toy without stepping off the unstable cushion.
activity_photo: [Image: Child balancing on a cushion while leaning to reach a toy]

description: 1. Balance a broomstick across two small stacks of books to create a low hurdle. 2. Ask the child to walk toward it. 3. They must balance on one leg momentarily while lifting the other leg high to clear the stick.
activity_photo: [Image: Child stepping high over a low hurdle]

activity: Catching a Ball While Sitting on a Yoga Ball
description: 1. Sit the child on a partially deflated yoga ball, holding their hips for safety. 2. Gently toss a balloon or soft ball to them. 3. They must engage their core to stay upright while reaching their arms out to catch.
activity_photo: [Image: Child sitting on a ball catching a balloon]

description: 1. Find a grassy hill or a safe, wide playground ramp. 2. Encourage the child to walk up the incline. 3. This forces them to adjust their center of gravity forward and engage their ankle stabilizers.
activity_photo: [Image: Child leaning forward to walk up a hill]

description: 1. Place a heavy ball (like a soccer ball) on the ground. 2. Tell the child to 'Kick it as hard as you can!' 3. The forceful swing of one leg requires intense stabilization from the standing leg to prevent falling.
activity_photo: [Image: Child balancing on one leg while kicking forcefully]

activity: Bending Down to Pick Up a Toy
description: 1. When the infant is standing and holding onto a low table, drop a toy at their feet. 2. Encourage them to look down. 3. Watch as they figure out how to bend their knees to retrieve it without falling over.
toy_photo: [Image: Toy on the floor next to a table]
activity_photo: [Image: Infant holding a table while bending to grab a toy]

activity: Walking While Carrying a Large Box
description: 1. Give the child a large, empty cardboard box that requires two arms to hold. 2. Have them walk across the room. 3. The bulky object obscures their vision of their feet and shifts their balance, requiring postural adjustments.
activity_photo: [Image: Child walking while holding a large box in front of them]

activity: Balancing a Beanbag on the Head
description: 1. Place a soft beanbag or a small rolled towel on top of the child's head. 2. Ask them to walk slowly to the other side of the room. 3. They must keep their neck and spine perfectly rigid and upright to prevent it from falling.
activity_photo: [Image: Child walking slowly with a beanbag on their head]

description: 1. Play fast music and encourage the child to run or dance wildly. 2. Pause the music and yell 'Freeze!' 3. The sudden halt requires immense muscle braking and immediate postural stabilization to avoid toppling.
activity_photo: [Image: Child freezing mid-dance in an awkward pose]

description: 1. Place a bin of toys on the floor. 2. Do not provide a chair. 3. Encourage the child to squat down (feet flat on floor, bottom resting near heels) to play, building deep core and leg endurance.
activity_photo: [Image: Child in a deep squat playing with blocks]

description: 1. Stand across the yard from the child. 2. Yell 'Green Light!' and wave them forward. 3. Yell 'Red Light!' and put your hand up; they must inhibit their desire to run and stop their body immediately.
activity_photo: [Image: Child running then freezing when parent puts hand up]

activity: Waiting for the Bell to Eat
description: 1. Place a desired snack in front of the child. 2. Tell them, 'You can eat it when you hear the bell ring.' 3. Wait 5-10 seconds, testing their impulse control, before ringing the bell.
activity_photo: [Image: Child staring at a snack waiting to eat it]

description: 1. Say, 'Let's see who can be quiet like a mouse the longest.' 2. Put your finger to your lips. 3. Praise the child for inhibiting their vocalizations and maintaining silence for 10-15 seconds.
activity_photo: [Image: Child with a finger over their lips staying quiet]

description: 1. Have the child sort blocks by Color (put all red here, all blue here). 2. Midway through, change the rule: 'Now, sort by Shape! Put all squares here, all circles here.' 3. They must mentally shift sets and abandon the old rule.
tools: Blocks of varying colors and shapes
activity_photo: [Image: Child pausing to think before sorting a new way]

description: 1. Blow a single bubble. 2. Tell the child, 'Let's watch it, but DO NOT pop it!' 3. They must actively suppress their strong motor impulse to reach out and pop the floating bubble.
activity_photo: [Image: Child holding hands back while watching a bubble land]

description: 1. Provide one drum and one mallet. 2. Hit the drum twice, then hold the mallet out. 3. The child must learn to wait while you play, and only play when it is their designated turn.
activity_photo: [Image: Child waiting patiently for parent to finish drumming]

description: 1. Explain the rules: Only do it if I say 'Simon Says'. 2. Say, 'Simon says touch your nose' (they do it). 3. Say, 'Touch your toes!' (they must inhibit the action because the magic words were missing).
activity_photo: [Image: Child stopping themselves from touching their toes]

description: 1. Set up a blanket fort and declare it the 'Whisper Cave'. 2. Enter the fort with the child. 3. They must continually remember the rule and inhibit their normal loud volume while inside the designated space.
activity_photo: [Image: Child whispering to a parent inside a fort]

description: 1. Wrap a small toy in tissue paper. 2. Set it on the table and tell the child, 'We will open this AFTER we finish our snack.' 3. They must delay gratification and keep their attention on the current task.
activity_photo: [Image: Child eating a snack while looking at a wrapped toy]

description: 1. Tell the child they are a turtle. 2. Instruct them to walk from the couch to the door as slowly as humanly possible. 3. They must actively suppress their natural, fast-paced motor rhythm to achieve the goal.
activity_photo: [Image: Child taking slow, exaggerated steps]

description: 1. Have the child close their eyes. 2. Place a sticker lightly on their forearm. 3. Tell them to open their eyes and immediately point to exactly where they felt the touch.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pointing to a sticker placed on their arm]

description: 1. Have the child close their eyes. 2. Gently brush a feather across their shin or knee. 3. Ask them to open their eyes and tap the exact spot where the feather touched them.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pointing to their knee after being tickled]

description: 1. Take a dab of baby lotion. 2. Rub it onto the back of the child's hand while they look away. 3. Ask them, 'Where is the wet lotion?' and have them rub that specific spot to blend it in.
activity_photo: [Image: Child rubbing lotion into the back of their hand]

description: 1. Have the child close their eyes tightly. 2. Say, 'Take your finger and touch your own nose!' 3. They must rely on internal maps of their body (proprioception) to find their face without visual guidance.
activity_photo: [Image: Child with eyes closed touching their nose]

description: 1. Lay the infant down. 2. Tap their foot and say 'Wake up, foot!' 3. Tap their tummy and say 'Wake up, tummy!', providing verbal labels mapped directly to tactile input on their body.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent tapping infant's tummy playfully]

description: 1. Stand facing the child. 2. Call out rapidly: 'Touch your ears! Touch your knees! Touch your belly!' 3. Watch to see how quickly they can locate and touch the named body parts on themselves.
activity_photo: [Image: Child touching their knees enthusiastically]

description: 1. Lay a piece of paper on the table. 2. Have the child place their hand flat on the paper. 3. Trace around their fingers with a crayon, showing them the 2D visual representation of their physical limb.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent tracing a child's hand on paper]

activity: Putting Hat on Head Without Looking
description: 1. Hand the child a knit winter hat. 2. Ask them to put it on their head. 3. They must lift their arms and guide the object to the top of their body using only spatial awareness, not a mirror.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pulling a hat down over their head]

description: 1. Take an ice cube wrapped in a thin towel. 2. Touch it briefly to the child's elbow or shoulder while they aren't looking. 3. Ask them, 'Where is it cold?' to test thermal localization.
activity_photo: [Image: Child grabbing their elbow where they felt cold]

description: 1. Pretend to bump your knee and say 'Ouch, my knee!' 2. Tell the child, 'Pretend you bumped your knee too. Show me where it hurts.' 3. Ensure they grab the correct joint on their own body.
activity_photo: [Image: Child rubbing their own knee pretending it hurts]

description: 1. Put the child in a very loose, oversized t-shirt. 2. Instruct them to cross their arms and grab the bottom hem. 3. Encourage them to pull the shirt all the way up and over their head independently.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pulling a shirt over their head]

description: 1. Hold the child's jacket open behind them. 2. Prompt them to reach one arm back and push it deep into the sleeve. 3. Have them reach the other arm back to find the second opening.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pushing arms back into coat sleeves]

description: 1. Put the child's shoes on their feet. 2. Leave the Velcro straps open. 3. Instruct the child to pull the strap tight across the top of their foot and press it down firmly to secure the shoe.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pressing a Velcro strap down on their shoe]

activity: Pulling Off Socks by the Toe
description: 1. Put loose-fitting socks on the child. 2. Show them how to pinch the fabric right at the toe. 3. Encourage them to pull straight outward to slip the sock completely off their foot.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pulling a sock off by the toe]

description: 1. Lay a pair of elastic-waist pants flat on the floor, front side up. 2. Have the child sit on the floor. 3. Instruct them to push one foot into each leg hole before trying to stand up.
activity_photo: [Image: Child sitting down pushing feet into pant legs]

description: 1. Cut soft fruit (like melon or banana) into bite-sized cubes. 2. Give the child a toddler-safe fork. 3. Show them how to aim and push downward forcefully to spear the food before lifting it to their mouth.
activity_photo: [Image: Child stabbing a piece of banana with a fork]

description: 1. Pour just one inch of water into a small, unbreakable open cup. 2. Guide the child to lift it to their mouth with both hands. 3. Help them tip it slowly to drink without spilling it down their chin.
activity_photo: [Image: Child carefully drinking from an open cup]

description: 1. When water spills, hand the child a dry towel. 2. Say, 'Uh oh, a spill. Can you wipe it up?' 3. Expect them to lay the towel over the water and pat or rub to absorb the mess.
activity_photo: [Image: Child wiping water off the floor with a towel]

description: 1. After a snack, hand the child an empty wrapper or napkin. 2. Point to the open trash can. 3. Instruct them to walk over and drop the garbage into the bin, participating in household cleanliness.
activity_photo: [Image: Child dropping a wrapper into a trash can]

activity: Carrying a Plate to the Sink
description: 1. When the child finishes eating, ask them to pick up their plastic plate. 2. Remind them to use two hands. 3. Have them walk slowly to the kitchen counter or sink and set it down gently.
activity_photo: [Image: Child carefully carrying a plate to the counter]

activity: Rolling a Ball to a Peer
description: 1. Sit the child on the floor facing a sibling or friend, legs spread wide. 2. Give one child a ball. 3. Guide them to push the ball so it rolls directly into the other child's lap, initiating turn-taking.
activity_photo: [Image: Two toddlers rolling a ball to each other]

description: 1. Tape two large pieces of paper next to each other on a table. 2. Provide washable paints. 3. Sit two children next to each other to paint. They may not interact much, but sharing the space is parallel play.
toy_photo: [Image: Two pieces of paper and paint pots]
activity_photo: [Image: Two children painting silently next to each other]

description: 1. When two children are playing with cars, suggest a trade. 2. Say, 'Can Billy play with the red car, and you play with the blue car?' 3. Facilitate the physical exchange of objects to build sharing skills.
activity_photo: [Image: Two children exchanging toy cars]

description: 1. Have the child hold hands with you and another person. 2. Walk in a circle singing the song. 3. When you say 'We all fall down!', everyone drops to the floor together, practicing coordinated group action.
toy_photo: [Image: Group of people holding hands icon]
activity_photo: [Image: Children holding hands falling to the floor laughing]

description: 1. Give two children a large pile of blocks to share. 2. Ask them to build one giant tower together. 3. They must negotiate space, take turns adding pieces, and work toward a common goal.
activity_photo: [Image: Two children adding blocks to the same tower]

description: 1. Play a simple game (like knocking over a block tower) with another person. 2. When the other person does it, clap your hands loudly and say 'Yay!' 3. Encourage the child to clap for others' successes.
activity_photo: [Image: Child clapping for a sibling who built a tower]

description: 1. Sit on the porch or look out the window with the infant. 2. When someone walks by, say 'Look, a friend! Let's wave.' 3. Take the infant's hand and gently wave it, modeling community greeting.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent helping infant wave out a window]

description: 1. Put a bandage on a teddy bear's leg. 2. Say, 'Oh no, the bear has a boo-boo. He is sad.' 3. Encourage the child to pat the bear, give it a hug, or offer it a blanket, fostering deep empathy.
activity_photo: [Image: Child hugging a teddy bear with a bandage]

description: 1. Sit in a circle with family members. 2. Give the child a bowl of crackers. 3. Ask them to take one, then pass the bowl to the person next to them, teaching group etiquette and sharing resources.
activity_photo: [Image: Child handing a bowl of snacks to their sibling]

description: 1. When you need to walk past the child and they are in the way, say gently, 'Excuse me, please.' 2. Prompt them to do the same when they try to squeeze past you, rather than pushing.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pausing to say 'excuse me' in a hallway]

description: 1. Gather red, blue, and yellow toys. 2. Set out three matching colored bowls. 3. Challenge the child to sort the toys into the three corresponding bowls, advancing their categorization skills.
tools: Red, blue, and yellow toys and bowls
activity_photo: [Image: Child placing a blue block into a blue bowl]

activity: Identifying the First Letter of Their Name
description: 1. Write the first letter of the child's name very large on a piece of paper. 2. Point to it and say, 'This is an M. M is for Mason!' 3. Ask them to trace it with their finger.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pointing to the first letter of their name]

description: 1. Hold the child's hands. 2. Tell them you are going to jump three times. 3. Jump together and count loudly: 'One! Two! Three! Stop.' Linking kinesthetic movement to rote counting.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent and child jumping together]

description: 1. Print pictures of a Cat, Hat, and Dog. 2. Say 'Cat sounds like Hat.' 3. Ask the child to hand you the two pictures that sound the same, introducing foundational phonemic awareness.
toy_photo: [Image: Flashcards of a cat and hat]
activity_photo: [Image: Child holding two rhyming picture cards]

description: 1. Draw a massive, thick number '1' on a chalkboard. 2. Give the child a piece of chalk. 3. Ask them to draw a line straight down right on top of yours, practicing early numeral formation.
activity_photo: [Image: Child drawing a line down on a chalkboard]

description: 1. Hand the child a familiar book, but hand it to them completely upside down. 2. Wait. 3. See if they recognize that the orientation is wrong and manually flip the book right-side up before opening it.
activity_photo: [Image: Child rotating an upside-down book to look at the cover]

description: 1. Tell the child it is time for a snack for them and a parent. 2. Hand them a stack of plates. 3. Say, 'We need TWO plates. Can you put two plates on the table?'
activity_photo: [Image: Child placing exactly two plates on a table]

description: 1. While walking or driving, point out a red octagonal Stop sign. 2. Explain that the red sign means 'Stop'. 3. Make a game of having the child shout 'Stop!' every time they spot the environmental print.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pointing at a stop sign outside]

description: 1. Place a pile of 10 blocks on the left and a pile of 2 blocks on the right. 2. Do not count them. 3. Ask the child, 'Which pile has MORE blocks?' building visual estimation of quantity.
toy_photo: [Image: A large pile and a small pile of blocks]
activity_photo: [Image: Child pointing to the larger pile of blocks]

description: 1. When washing hands, start singing the ABC song. 2. Encourage the child to sing along. 3. Teach them that they must keep scrubbing until the song is over, linking literacy to a hygiene timer.
activity_photo: [Image: Child washing hands while singing]

description: 1. Stand the child on a bottom stair tread or a sturdy 4-inch block. 2. Stand in front of them holding their hands. 3. Say '1, 2, 3, Jump!' and encourage them to launch off with both feet simultaneously.
activity_photo: [Image: Child jumping off a small step holding parent's hands]

description: 1. Demonstrate a galloping motion (one foot always leading, the other trailing and catching up). 2. Tell the child to 'Ride the horse!' 3. Have them practice this asymmetrical, rhythmic movement across the yard.
activity_photo: [Image: Child attempting to gallop across a lawn]

description: 1. Tape a thick, straight line on the floor. 2. Instruct the child to stand on the line. 3. Have them walk backward, trying to keep their feet on the tape without turning around to look.
activity_photo: [Image: Child walking carefully backward along a line]

description: 1. Give the child a small tennis ball or rolled sock. 2. Show them how to raise their arm up past their ear. 3. Instruct them to throw the ball forcefully overhand, rather than underhand tossing.
activity_photo: [Image: Child cocking their arm back for an overhand throw]

description: 1. Stand about 10 feet away from the child. 2. Roll a large playground ball smoothly toward them. 3. The child must time their run-up and swing their leg to kick the ball while it is still moving.
activity_photo: [Image: Child stepping forward to kick a rolling ball]

description: 1. Stand safely behind the child at a playground. 2. Guide them to grip the rungs of a low, slanted ladder or rock wall. 3. Encourage them to pull with their arms and push with their legs to climb upward.
activity_photo: [Image: Child climbing a playground ladder with parent spotting]

description: 1. Sit the child on a toddler tricycle. 2. Physically place their feet flat on the pedals. 3. Hold their feet in place and push the trike slowly forward so they feel the circular motion of pedaling.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent holding child's feet on tricycle pedals]

description: 1. Tell the child to 'Stand up tall like a ballerina!' 2. Show them how to lift their heels off the ground. 3. Encourage them to take a few steps walking only on their tiptoes, requiring intense calf control.
activity_photo: [Image: Child walking carefully on their tiptoes]

activity: Crawling Over Pillows with Toy in Hand
description: 1. Lay out a pile of couch cushions. 2. Have the child hold a toy car in one hand. 3. They must crawl over the unstable cushions using a 'three-point crawl' because one hand is occupied, challenging their balance.
toy_photo: [Image: Assorted pillows and a toy car]
activity_photo: [Image: Child crawling over pillows while clutching a toy]

description: 1. Stand facing the child. 2. Lift one of your knees high into the air like a flamingo. 3. Tell them to try it! Watch them shift their weight to balance on a single leg for 1 to 2 seconds.
activity_photo: [Image: Child lifting one leg to balance momentarily]

description: 1. Play a song with a strong, slow 4/4 marching beat. 2. Exaggerate lifting your knees high to the rhythm. 3. Encourage the child to follow you around the room, matching their steps to the music.
activity_photo: [Image: Child marching happily behind a parent]

description: 1. Give the child two wooden rhythm sticks or unsharpened pencils. 2. Tap a simple 'one-two' rhythm. 3. Ask them to listen and repeat the exact tapping speed and pattern back to you.
activity_photo: [Image: Child hitting two sticks together]

description: 1. Sit with the infant on your lap facing you. 2. Sing a lullaby and rock them very slowly. 3. Switch to a lively song and bounce them quickly, helping them physically feel tempo changes.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent bouncing baby to a fast tempo]

description: 1. Give the child a lightweight chiffon scarf. 2. Put on slow, classical music. 3. Instruct them to move the scarf smoothly and fluidly, matching the drawn-out tempo of the song.
activity_photo: [Image: Child swaying smoothly with a scarf]

description: 1. Tell the child to crouch down low. 2. Say, 'When I clap loudly, jump up like a frog!' 3. Clap your hands randomly; they must anticipate and time their physical jump to match your auditory cue.
activity_photo: [Image: Child leaping up the moment a parent claps]

description: 1. Give the child a bowl of water and a whisk. 2. Sing 'Row, Row, Row Your Boat'. 3. Encourage them to stir the water in circles, matching the speed of their arm to the speed of your singing.
activity_photo: [Image: Child stirring water rhythmically]

description: 1. Set a lump of playdough in front of the child. 2. Count '1, 2, 3, SMASH!' 3. The child must hold their hand ready and strike the dough exactly on the word 'Smash'.
activity_photo: [Image: Child smashing dough right on cue]

activity: Passing a Ball on the Beat
description: 1. Sit facing the child. 2. Say 'Pass, pass, pass' in a steady rhythm. 3. Roll the ball back and forth, timing the release of the ball so it crosses the floor right on the beat.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent and child rolling a ball back and forth on a beat]

description: 1. Stand with the child. 2. Say 'Left, Right, Left, Right' while stomping heavily. 3. Encourage them to shift their weight and stomp the corresponding foot in a steady, alternating rhythm.
activity_photo: [Image: Child stomping feet alternately]

activity: Shaking Eggs to Stop and Go
description: 1. Give the child two plastic shaker eggs. 2. Say 'Go!' and shake rapidly. 3. Say 'Stop!' and freeze immediately, teaching them to align their motor actions with sudden rhythmic stops.
activity_photo: [Image: Child frozen with shakers mid-air]

description: 1. Lay the infant on their back in a dimly lit room. 2. Shine a flashlight onto the ceiling directly above them. 3. Move the beam slowly in a large circle, encouraging their eyes to follow the light smoothly.
activity_photo: [Image: Infant tracking a light beam on the ceiling]

description: 1. Hold a large craft feather high above the child's head. 2. Drop it. 3. Encourage them to watch it gently drift left and right until it hits the floor without moving their whole head.
activity_photo: [Image: Child watching a feather float to the ground]

description: 1. Set up a plastic marble run toy. 2. Drop a bright marble in the top. 3. Ask the child to keep their eyes on the marble as it zig-zags down the complex path.
activity_photo: [Image: Child intently watching a marble roll down a track]

description: 1. Tie a bright toy to a string. 2. Hold it in front of the infant's face (about 12 inches away). 3. Swing it gently side-to-side like a pendulum so their eyes cross the midline to track it.
activity_photo: [Image: Infant's eyes following a swinging toy]

activity: Rolling a Car Across a Table
description: 1. Have the child sit at a wide table so the surface is at eye level. 2. Quickly roll a toy car horizontally from left to right. 3. They must use smooth pursuit eye movements to track the fast object.
activity_photo: [Image: Child tracking a car rolling across a table]

description: 1. Take a brightly colored play scarf. 2. Toss it straight up into the air. 3. The child must watch it fall and reach out to catch it right before it touches the ground.
activity_photo: [Image: Child reaching to catch a falling scarf]

description: 1. Hold a colorful pinwheel in front of the child. 2. Have them blow on it to make it spin. 3. The rapid rotation of the colors forces their eyes to attempt to stabilize and track the moving pattern.
activity_photo: [Image: Child watching a spinning pinwheel]

description: 1. Turn on a laser pointer or a strong focused flashlight beam. 2. Move it quickly across the floor. 3. Ask the child to chase it and 'stomp on the bug!', linking rapid eye tracking to gross motor action.
activity_photo: [Image: Child trying to stomp on a moving light beam]

description: 1. Blow up a balloon but do not tie it. 2. Say 'Watch it go!' and let it go. 3. The child must rapidly move their eyes to track the erratic, unpredictable flight path of the deflating balloon.
activity_photo: [Image: Child watching a balloon fly erratically around a room]

description: 1. Hold your index finger up about a foot from the infant's face. 2. Slowly draw a large figure-eight in the air. 3. Ensure their eyes follow the complete continuous path without looking away.
activity_photo: [Image: Infant tracking parent's finger in the air]

description: 1. Give the child a teddy bear, an empty plastic bowl, and a spoon. 2. Say, 'The bear is hungry! Can you feed him soup?' 3. Encourage them to pretend to scoop and feed the inanimate object.
toy_photo: [Image: Teddy bear with a bowl and spoon]
activity_photo: [Image: Child pretending to feed a teddy bear]

activity: Using a Block as a Phone
description: 1. Pick up a simple wooden block. 2. Hold it to your ear and say 'Hello? Yes, I'm here.' 3. Hand it to the child; they must assign a new, symbolic identity (a phone) to the block to continue the play.
activity_photo: [Image: Child holding a block to their ear chatting]

description: 1. Provide a baby doll and a small hand towel (as a blanket). 2. Tell the child the baby is tired. 3. Have them lay the doll down, cover it with the towel, and say 'Shh', practicing complex pretend routines.
activity_photo: [Image: Child tucking a baby doll in with a towel]

description: 1. Hand the child a simple plastic plate or a frisbee. 2. Sit next to them and hold one too. 3. Say, 'Let's drive to the park!' and turn the plate left and right while making car noises.
activity_photo: [Image: Child holding a plate pretending to drive]

description: 1. Turn a medium cardboard box upside down to act as a 'stove'. 2. Give the child a pot and wooden spoon. 3. Encourage them to place the pot on the box and 'cook dinner' for the family.
toy_photo: [Image: Upside down box and a pot]
activity_photo: [Image: Child stirring a pot on top of a cardboard box]

activity: Doctor Checkup on a Stuffed Animal
description: 1. Provide a toy stethoscope or just a short piece of string. 2. Say 'The doggy has a cough.' 3. Instruct the child to use the tool to 'listen' to the stuffed animal's heart and give it a checkup.
activity_photo: [Image: Child using a toy stethoscope on a stuffed dog]

description: 1. Set up a toy tea set or just use two empty plastic cups. 2. Pretend to pour hot tea into the cups. 3. Exaggerate blowing on it to cool it down, then take a sip and say 'Ahhh!' Encourage the child to mimic.
activity_photo: [Image: Child taking a sip from an empty cup]

description: 1. Give the child a standard broom. 2. Show them how to place it between their legs. 3. Tell them it's a horse and encourage them to gallop around the yard shouting 'Yee-haw!', turning a tool into a toy.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pretending to ride a broomstick]

description: 1. Give the child a reusable grocery tote bag. 2. Scatter a few clean, empty food boxes (like a cereal box) on the floor. 3. Tell them to 'go shopping' and place the items into their bag.
toy_photo: [Image: Tote bag and a cereal box]
