activity_photo: [Image: Child placing an empty box into a tote bag]

activity: Fixing it with a Toy Hammer
description: 1. Point to a leg of a chair or a table. 2. Hand the child a plastic toy hammer. 3. Say, 'Oh no, the chair is broken! Can you fix it?' and let them tap the leg to 'repair' it.
activity_photo: [Image: Child tapping a chair leg with a toy hammer]

description: 1. Place half a peeled banana on a plate. 2. Hand the child a dull fork. 3. Instead of stabbing, show them how to use the back of the fork to push down and mash the food into a paste.
activity_photo: [Image: Child mashing a banana with the back of a fork]

description: 1. Roll playdough into a long 'snake'. 2. Give the child a pair of blunt, plastic safety scissors. 3. Show them how to squeeze the handles to snip the soft dough into little pieces, introducing scissor skills safely.
activity_photo: [Image: Child snipping playdough with plastic scissors]

description: 1. Place a few flat, thin coasters or pieces of cardboard on the floor. 2. Give the child a clean kitchen spatula. 3. Ask them to slide the spatula under the 'pancakes' and flip them over.
activity_photo: [Image: Child using a spatula to flip a coaster over]

description: 1. Fill a small bin with kinetic sand or dry rice. 2. Give the child a large serving spoon and a small cup. 3. They must use the spoon as a tool to transfer the material from the bin into the cup.
activity_photo: [Image: Child scooping sand with a large spoon]

activity: Wiping a Board with an Eraser
description: 1. Scribble on a small whiteboard with a dry-erase marker. 2. Hand the child a felt eraser. 3. Instruct them to grip the block and wipe it back and forth to clear the board.
activity_photo: [Image: Child rubbing an eraser over a whiteboard]

description: 1. Place a bowl of large craft pom-poms on the table. 2. Give the child a pair of small, easy-to-squeeze kitchen tongs. 3. Have them use the tool to extract the soft items and drop them in an empty bowl.
activity_photo: [Image: Child squeezing tongs to pick up a pom-pom]

description: 1. Clean out an empty, plastic peanut butter jar. 2. Place the lid loosely on top. 3. Have the child hold the jar with one hand and use the other to twist the lid clockwise to seal it shut.
toy_photo: [Image: Clear plastic jar with a lid]
activity_photo: [Image: Child twisting a lid tightly onto a plastic jar]

description: 1. Go outside and fill a paint tray with plain water. 2. Give the child a small, clean foam paint roller. 3. Show them how to dip it and roll it up and down the concrete or fence to 'paint' it wet.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pushing a wet paint roller against a fence]

description: 1. Cut a standard kitchen sponge into a small square. 2. Provide a shallow dish of washable paint and a piece of paper. 3. The child must grip the sponge, dip it, and press it firmly to the paper as a stamp.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pressing a painted sponge onto paper]

description: 1. Fill a small, child-sized watering can with an inch of water. 2. Walk them over to a potted plant. 3. Instruct them to tip the spout over the dirt to water the plant, controlling the flow of a tool.
activity_photo: [Image: Child tipping a watering can over a plant]

description: 1. Have the infant sit on the floor. 2. Stand slightly behind them to the left. 3. Shake a rattle loudly. They must quickly turn their head and eyes to the exact location of the auditory input.
activity_photo: [Image: Infant turning head sharply to find a sound behind them]

description: 1. Hide a ticking watch or a softly playing phone in one of your closed hands. 2. Hold both fists out to the child. 3. They must put their ear close to your hands to localize the sound and pick the correct one.
activity_photo: [Image: Child putting their ear near a closed fist to listen]

activity: Finding Mom's Voice in the Dark
description: 1. Turn the lights off or dim them heavily. 2. Walk to the corner of the room. 3. Softly call the child's name; they must navigate the space relying solely on their hearing to find you.
activity_photo: [Image: Child walking toward a voice in a dark room]

description: 1. Have the child close their eyes. 2. Shake a tambourine high above their head, then stop. 3. Ask, 'Was the sound up high or down low?' They must interpret spatial orientation from sound alone.
activity_photo: [Image: Child with eyes closed pointing up toward a sound]

description: 1. Have the child crawl on the floor. 2. Walk slowly in front of them ringing a bell continuously. 3. They must crawl after the sound, tracking the moving auditory target.
activity_photo: [Image: Child crawling after a ringing bell]

description: 1. Stand directly behind the child while they keep their eyes forward. 2. Lean in and whisper a word into their left ear. 3. Ask them to point to which ear heard the secret.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pointing to their left ear]

description: 1. Have the child sit facing away from you. 2. Bounce a heavy ball loudly on the floor to their left or right side. 3. They must turn around and point to where they think the ball hit the ground.
activity_photo: [Image: Child turning around pointing to the floor]

description: 1. Wind up a music box or turn on a musical toy. 2. Hide it under a blanket or behind a pillow while the child isn't looking. 3. Tell them to use their ears to hunt down the hidden music.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pulling a pillow away to find a noisy toy]

description: 1. Lay the infant on their back. 2. Snap your fingers near their right ear, then quickly over their left shoulder. 3. Watch them shift their gaze and head position quickly to locate the sharp sounds.
activity_photo: [Image: Infant looking side to side to track finger snaps]

activity: Dropping a Coin in a Cup
description: 1. Place three opaque cups upside down on the table. 2. Lift one and drop a coin under it so it clinks, while the child's eyes are closed. 3. Have them open their eyes and point to the cup that made the noise.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pointing to a cup after hearing a clink]

activity: Which Cup is Hiding the Toy?
description: 1. Show the child a small toy car. 2. Place it under one of two distinct, different colored cups. 3. Wait 5 seconds, talking about something else, then ask them to lift the cup holding the toy.
activity_photo: [Image: Child lifting a blue cup to find a hidden car]

description: 1. Lay three colored mats on the floor (e.g., Red, Blue, Green). 2. Jump on them in a sequence (Red, then Green). 3. Ask the child to copy the exact spatial path you took without stepping on the Blue.
activity_photo: [Image: Child jumping from a red mat to a green mat]

activity: Putting the Toy Back on the Shelf
description: 1. Take a book off the bottom shelf of a bookcase. 2. Read it together on the couch. 3. When finished, ask the child to go put it back in the exact spot it came from, testing spatial recall.
activity_photo: [Image: Child placing a book onto the correct bottom shelf]

description: 1. Place a shape puzzle in front of the child. 2. Remove three pieces (circle, square, triangle). 3. Show them the triangle and ask, 'Which hole does this go in?' They must recall the spatial layout of the board.
activity_photo: [Image: Child holding a triangle piece looking at a puzzle board]

description: 1. While the child watches, place their favorite blanket behind the living room chair. 2. Leave the room together for a minute. 3. Return and ask, 'Where did we put your blanket?'
activity_photo: [Image: Child walking directly behind a chair to grab their blanket]

description: 1. Use two identical picture cards and one different card. 2. Lay them face down. 3. Flip one identical card over to show them, turn it back, and ask them to find its match by remembering its spatial position.
activity_photo: [Image: Child flipping over a card to find a match]

activity: Which Hand is the Penny In?
description: 1. Put a penny in your left hand. 2. Close both fists and cross your arms over your chest while the child watches. 3. Ask them to point to the hand with the penny, tracking the spatial movement of your arms.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pointing to a parent's crossed arm]

description: 1. Line up a Red, Blue, and Green block in a row. 2. Have the child look at it, then cover it with a towel. 3. Give them their own Red, Blue, and Green blocks and ask them to build the same sequence from memory.
toy_photo: [Image: Red, blue, and green blocks in a line]
activity_photo: [Image: Child trying to arrange blocks in a specific order]

description: 1. Open a specific drawer in the kitchen and show the child where the spoons are kept. 2. Close it. 3. Ask them, 'Can you open the drawer with the spoons?' They must recall the specific vertical location.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pulling open the correct drawer]

description: 1. Play peek-a-boo, but duck down behind the couch. 2. Pop up and say 'Boo!', then duck down again. 3. Wait to see if the child crawls directly to the spatial location behind the couch to find you.
activity_photo: [Image: Child crawling around a couch looking for parent]

description: 1. Place a piece of paper on a smooth table. 2. Give the child a crayon. 3. The child must use their non-dominant hand to press down and stabilize the paper while their dominant hand moves to draw.
activity_photo: [Image: Child holding paper still with one hand while drawing with the other]

description: 1. Provide a large wooden or plastic lacing needle and a stiff shoelace. 2. The child must hold the needle perfectly still with one hand while the other hand maneuvers the floppy lace through the eye.
activity_photo: [Image: Child concentrating to thread a lace through a large needle]

description: 1. Give the child a small plastic pitcher half-filled with water. 2. Place an empty cup on the table. 3. They must hold the cup steady with one hand while lifting and tilting the pitcher with the other.
activity_photo: [Image: Child holding a cup and pouring water into it]

description: 1. Hand the child a sealed plastic sandwich bag containing a snack. 2. They must grasp one side of the top lip with one hand and pull the other side in the opposite direction to break the seal.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pulling apart the top of a ziploc bag]

description: 1. Give the child a mixing bowl with a little water and a spoon. 2. Show them how the bowl spins if they don't hold it. 3. They must actively grip the rim with one hand while stirring vigorously with the other.
activity_photo: [Image: Child holding a bowl steady while stirring]

description: 1. Hand the child a tube of toothpaste and a toothbrush. 2. They must hold the narrow brush steady in one hand while applying targeted squeezing pressure to the tube with the other hand.
activity_photo: [Image: Child attempting to squeeze paste onto a brush]

description: 1. Provide a heavy desk tape dispenser. 2. The child must pull the tape out with their dominant hand, then use a specialized downward twisting motion against the metal teeth while stabilizing the roll.
activity_photo: [Image: Child ripping a piece of tape off a dispenser]

description: 1. Start the tear at the top of a banana. 2. Hand it to the child. 3. They must grip the base of the fruit firmly in one fist while using their other hand to pinch and pull the peel downward.
activity_photo: [Image: Child holding a banana and pulling the peel down]

description: 1. Give the child a lightweight plastic shape sorter box. 2. When they try to push a tight block in, the box will move. 3. They must learn to press down on the top of the box with one hand while pushing the block with the other.
activity_photo: [Image: Child holding a sorter box steady to push a shape in]

description: 1. Stick a long piece of painter's tape to the edge of a table. 2. Instruct the child to tear it in half. 3. They must pinch the tape with both hands close together, pulling one hand towards them and pushing the other away.
activity_photo: [Image: Child tearing a strip of tape in half]

description: 1. Crush chocolate graham crackers into a fine dust to look like dirt. 2. Place it in a bin. 3. Let the child explore the 'dirt' with their hands, and encourage them to taste it, learning that visual appearances can be surprising.
activity_photo: [Image: Child licking chocolate 'dirt' off their fingers]

description: 1. Cut a small, fresh wedge of lemon. 2. Have the child stick their tongue out and lightly touch it to the fruit. 3. Discuss the intense 'sour' reaction and the physical sensation of puckering.
activity_photo: [Image: Child making a sour, puckered face]

description: 1. Give the child a thick pretzel stick coated in coarse salt. 2. Instruct them to lick the outside before biting it. 3. Help them identify the sharp, savory taste of 'salty' on their tongue.
activity_photo: [Image: Child licking salt off a pretzel]

description: 1. Open a bottle of baking vanilla extract. 2. Hold it a few inches from the child's nose. 3. Instruct them to take a gentle sniff, introducing them to strong, sweet, concentrated aromas.
activity_photo: [Image: Child leaning in to smell a bottle]

activity: Blind Taste Test: Sweet or Sour?
description: 1. Have the child close their eyes. 2. Place a small piece of sweet fruit (like a grape) on their tongue. 3. Ask them, 'Is it sweet like candy, or sour like a lemon?' relying entirely on taste to answer.
activity_photo: [Image: Child with eyes closed chewing a piece of fruit]

description: 1. Mix a heavy dash of cinnamon powder into a batch of playdough. 2. Give it to the child. 3. Every time they squish or pull it, encourage them to smell the spicy aroma released by the manipulation.
activity_photo: [Image: Child holding playdough up to their nose]

description: 1. Pluck a fresh mint leaf from a garden or grocery pack. 2. Show the child how to rub the leaf vigorously between their fingers to release the oils. 3. Have them smell their fingertips to discover the sharp, cooling scent.
activity_photo: [Image: Child rubbing a leaf and smelling their fingers]

description: 1. Provide a plate with a hard carrot stick and a scoop of applesauce. 2. Have the child bite the carrot to hear the 'crunch' in their head. 3. Have them eat the applesauce to feel the 'mushy' texture, comparing auditory/tactile eating sensations.
activity_photo: [Image: Child biting a hard carrot stick]

description: 1. Place a few whole roasted coffee beans in a small cup. 2. Let the child hold the cup and shake it slightly. 3. Have them put their nose near the rim to smell the bitter, earthy, adult aroma.
activity_photo: [Image: Child sniffing a cup of coffee beans]

description: 1. Pour milk into two small cups. Leave one cold and warm the other slightly in the microwave. 2. Have the child sip the cold milk, then immediately sip the warm milk. 3. Discuss how temperature changes the experience of a familiar taste.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pointing to a cup of warm milk]

description: 1. Give the child a large loop of masking tape with the sticky side facing out. 2. Tell them to tap it with their fingers. 3. Discuss the 'sticky' feeling as they pull their fingers away against the resistance.
activity_photo: [Image: Child's fingers pulling away from sticky tape]

description: 1. Guide the infant's hand to smack a hard wooden floor or table. 2. Say 'Hard!'. 3. Immediately guide their hand to smack a soft, fluffy pillow and say 'Soft!', creating extreme tactile contrast.
toy_photo: [Image: Wooden block and a small pillow]
activity_photo: [Image: Infant patting a soft pillow]

description: 1. Place a smooth rubber ball and a textured/bumpy massage ball inside a dark bag. 2. Tell the child to reach in without looking. 3. Ask them to feel around and only pull out the 'bumpy' one.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pulling a spiky ball out of a bag]

activity: Walking on Rough Carpet vs. Tile
description: 1. Take off the child's socks. 2. Have them walk on a smooth, cold kitchen tile floor. 3. Have them walk immediately onto a rough, warm carpet, talking about what the bottoms of their feet are feeling.
activity_photo: [Image: Child looking at their bare feet on a tile floor]

description: 1. Place an ice cube in a bowl. 2. Encourage the child to pick it up with their bare hands. 3. They must experience the extreme cold and the slippery, melting texture, describing it as 'cold' or 'wet'.
activity_photo: [Image: Child quickly dropping a cold ice cube into a bowl]

description: 1. Take a soft feather. 2. Gently drag it down the infant's cheek and neck. 3. Observe their reaction to the ultra-light, ticklish tactile input, which is very different from a firm touch or hug.
activity_photo: [Image: Infant giggling as a feather touches their cheek]

description: 1. Provide a small square of medium-grit sandpaper. 2. Instruct the child to rub their thumb lightly over the surface. 3. Use the word 'rough' or 'scratchy' to label this specific abrasive sensation.
activity_photo: [Image: Child rubbing their thumb on sandpaper]

description: 1. Put a spoonful of plain, cool hair gel or aloe vera in a ziploc bag and seal it. 2. Have the child press it flat. 3. Then, put a dollop directly on their hands so they can feel the 'slimy' texture without the plastic barrier.
activity_photo: [Image: Child squishing cold gel between their fingers]

description: 1. Fill one identical small opaque plastic container with heavy rocks, and another with light cotton. 2. Seal the lids. 3. Have the child lift both to feel the difference in density and weight, identifying the 'heavy' one.
activity_photo: [Image: Child lifting a surprisingly heavy tub]

description: 1. Provide two identical washcloths. Soak one in water and wring it out; leave the other dry. 2. Have the child touch the dry one and say 'Dry'. 3. Have them touch the damp one and say 'Wet', feeling the moisture difference.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pressing hands on a wet cloth]

description: 1. Allow a toy block to fall into a narrow gap behind the couch where the child's arm cannot fit. 2. Give them a yardstick or a long tube. 3. Let them figure out how to use the long tool to sweep the block out from the gap.
activity_photo: [Image: Child using a stick to reach behind a sofa]

description: 1. Present a tightly stacked tower of three nesting cups. 2. To get to the bottom cup, the infant must realize they cannot pull the bottom one out; they must remove the top two first.
activity_photo: [Image: Infant pulling the top cup off a stack]

description: 1. Loosely tie a thick, soft rope or scarf around the handle of a basket containing a toy. 2. The child must figure out how to pull the loops of the loose knot apart to free the toy.
tools: Thick rope or scarf, basket, toy
activity_photo: [Image: Child manipulating a knot to untie it]

activity: Retrieving Toy Under a Clear Bowl
description: 1. Place a bright toy on the floor. 2. Turn a clear, heavy glass or plastic bowl upside down over the toy. 3. The infant can see the toy, but must solve the physical barrier problem by lifting or pushing the heavy bowl away.
toy_photo: [Image: Toy trapped under a clear bowl]
activity_photo: [Image: Infant trying to lift a heavy bowl to get a toy]

description: 1. Place a large plastic key onto a binder ring or a large shower curtain ring. 2. Snap it closed. 3. The child must examine the ring, figure out the hinge/opening mechanism, and pull it apart to get the key.
activity_photo: [Image: Child trying to pull a binder ring open]

description: 1. Give the child a large wooden block. 2. Present one small box and one large box. 3. Ask them to put the block away; they must visually measure and test to realize it will only fit in the large box.
tools: Large block, big box, small box
toy_photo: [Image: Large block and two cardboard boxes]
activity_photo: [Image: Child trying to shove a big block into a tiny box]

description: 1. Tape a few small plastic animals flat to a baking sheet using strong masking tape. 2. The child cannot simply pick the animal up; they must figure out how to scratch and peel the tape back to free the toy.
tools: Baking sheet, masking tape, plastic animals
toy_photo: [Image: Plastic toy taped to a metal pan]
activity_photo: [Image: Child picking at the edge of tape to free a toy]

description: 1. Place a soft toy on a high shelf. 2. Give the child a mechanical 'claw grabber' toy. 3. They must figure out how to extend the tool, position the claw, and squeeze the handle to retrieve the out-of-reach item.
activity_photo: [Image: Child using a claw grabber to reach a high shelf]

activity: Turning the Tube to Get the Ball
description: 1. Show the child a clear plastic tube (like from a poster). 2. Drop a small ball into the center so it rests in the middle. 3. Hand them the tube horizontally; they must realize they have to tilt it vertically for gravity to drop the ball out.
toy_photo: [Image: Clear tube with a ball stuck inside]
activity_photo: [Image: Child tilting a tube to make a ball roll out]

description: 1. Set out a small round Tupperware, a large round Tupperware, and a square Tupperware. 2. Hand the child the small round lid. 3. They must use trial and error, rotating and pressing, to figure out which container the lid seals onto.
tools: Three mismatched Tupperware containers, one lid
activity_photo: [Image: Child testing a round lid on a square container]

description: 1. Stick several strips of painter's tape to a wall at the child's eye level. 2. Fold the ends over slightly to make a tab. 3. Encourage the child to use a pincer grasp to peel the tape off, building wrist extension and shoulder stability.
activity_photo: [Image: Child peeling tape off a wall]

description: 1. Provide a plastic piggy bank and a handful of large plastic play coins. 2. Have the child hold a coin using their thumb and index finger. 3. Instruct them to visually align the thin edge of the coin with the narrow slot to drop it in.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pushing a coin into a slot]

description: 1. Turn a kitchen colander upside down. 2. Give the child a handful of stiff pipe cleaners. 3. Show them how to carefully thread the pipe cleaners into the tiny holes to create a colorful 'porcupine'.
toy_photo: [Image: Metal colander and colorful pipe cleaners]
activity_photo: [Image: Child threading pipe cleaners into a colander]

description: 1. Provide two bowls during water play: one full of water, one empty. 2. Give the child a large, soft sponge. 3. Have them soak the sponge in the full bowl, move it over the empty bowl, and squeeze with both hands to extract the water.
activity_photo: [Image: Child squeezing a wet sponge into a bowl]

description: 1. Stick a dozen colorful Post-it notes on a wall. 2. Tell the child to collect them all. 3. They must peel the note off with one hand and transfer it to the palm of their other hand, holding a growing stack.
activity_photo: [Image: Child collecting sticky notes off a wall]

description: 1. Take an empty tissue box and stuff it with small square scraps of fabric or play scarves. 2. Pull the tip of one fabric piece through the top slot. 3. Encourage the infant to pinch the fabric and pull it all the way out.
toy_photo: [Image: Tissue box with colorful scarves inside]
activity_photo: [Image: Infant pulling a scarf out of a box]

description: 1. Hand the child a thick-paged board book. 2. Sit next to them. 3. Instruct them to turn the pages one at a time, preventing them from grabbing 'chunks' of pages, which requires refined finger isolation.
activity_photo: [Image: Child carefully turning a single thick page]

description: 1. Flatten a large pancake of playdough on the table. 2. Show the child how to point their index finger while keeping their other fingers tucked in. 3. Have them poke deep holes all over the playdough using only that pointer finger.
activity_photo: [Image: Child poking holes in playdough with one finger]

description: 1. Wrap several small plastic animals tightly in aluminum foil to look like silver rocks. 2. Hand them to the child. 3. They must use both hands to pull, tear, and peel the foil away to discover the hidden toy.
activity_photo: [Image: Child tearing foil off a hidden toy]

description: 1. Firmly snap two large, interlocking plastic blocks (like Duplo) together. 2. Give the stuck pair to the child. 3. Instruct them to grip tightly and pull with their arm and chest muscles to separate the pieces.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pulling hard to separate two blocks]

description: 1. Lay a broomstick flat on the floor, or prop it up slightly on two books. 2. Ask the child to walk toward it. 3. They must lift their knee high and balance on one foot momentarily to step cleanly over the obstacle.
activity_photo: [Image: Child stepping high over a broom handle]

activity: Kicking a Tower of Blocks Down
description: 1. Build a tall tower out of large, soft foam blocks. 2. Have the child stand back. 3. Say '1, 2, 3, Kick!' and encourage them to swing their leg forcefully to knock the tower down, practicing target kicking.
activity_photo: [Image: Child kicking a foam block tower over]

activity: Crawling Through a Cardboard Box Tunnel
description: 1. Open both ends of a large moving box. 2. Place a toy at the far end. 3. Encourage the child to get on their hands and knees and crawl through the enclosed, narrow space, building spatial body awareness.
activity_photo: [Image: Child crawling through a box tunnel]

description: 1. Put a few heavy towels or books in a plastic laundry basket on a carpeted floor. 2. Tell the child they are a bulldozer. 3. Have them lean their body weight against the basket and push it across the room.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pushing a heavy basket across a carpet]

description: 1. Stand facing the child and hold both of their hands. 2. Take a step toward them and say 'Step back.' 3. Practice walking backward together safely, which develops unique balancing muscles.
activity_photo: [Image: Child walking backward holding parent's hands]

description: 1. Tape a large sheet of big-pocket bubble wrap to the floor. 2. Instruct the child to jump and stomp with both feet. 3. The gross motor impact is rewarded with loud auditory pops, encouraging heavier stomping.
activity_photo: [Image: Child stomping barefoot on bubble wrap]

activity: Reaching Up to Touch a Hanging Balloon
description: 1. Hang a balloon from a doorway using a string, positioning it just above the child's reach. 2. Encourage them to stretch their arms up high and get on their tiptoes to tap the balloon.
activity_photo: [Image: Child reaching high on tiptoes to touch a balloon]

activity: Bear Crawling Across the Living Room
description: 1. Show the child how to do a 'bear crawl': hands and feet flat on the floor, bottom sticking up in the air. 2. Have a race across the room in this position, which heavily engages the core and shoulders.
activity_photo: [Image: Child bear crawling across a rug]

description: 1. Place a firm, flat couch cushion on the floor. 2. Have the child stand on top of it. 3. Hold their hands and say 'Jump!' encouraging them to launch forward with both feet landing at the same time.
activity_photo: [Image: Child jumping off a cushion holding hands]

activity: Balancing on One Foot while Holding Hands
description: 1. Stand facing the child and hold both of their hands securely. 2. Lift one of your own legs. 3. Tell the child to 'Be a flamingo!' and help them lift one leg, holding the balance for 3 seconds.
activity_photo: [Image: Child balancing on one leg holding parent's hands]

description: 1. Boil spaghetti, rinse it in cold water, and let it cool. Place it in a large bowl. 2. Hide a few plastic toys inside the noodles. 3. Let the child plunge their hands in to feel the cold, slippery, slimy texture.
activity_photo: [Image: Child's hands covered in cold spaghetti]

description: 1. Take the child to a clean sandbox or the beach. 2. Remove their shoes and socks. 3. Encourage them to walk, stand, and bury their toes in the dry, gritty sand, providing intense input to the feet.
activity_photo: [Image: Child standing barefoot in sand]

description: 1. Open distinct, safe spice jars from the kitchen (e.g., cinnamon, vanilla, mint). 2. Hold the jar near the child's nose. 3. Ask them to take a big sniff and talk about whether the smell is sweet or spicy.
activity_photo: [Image: Child leaning in to smell a jar of cinnamon]

activity: Tasting Sweet vs. Sour (Banana vs. Lemon)
description: 1. Place a piece of sweet banana and a small wedge of sour lemon on a plate. 2. Have the child taste the banana and say 'Sweet.' 3. Have them taste the lemon and observe the physical 'pucker' reaction to the sour taste.
toy_photo: [Image: Slice of banana and slice of lemon]
activity_photo: [Image: Child puckering their lips after tasting lemon]

activity: Feeling Rough Sandpaper and Smooth Silk
description: 1. Provide a square of rough sandpaper and a silky scarf. 2. Have the child rub their hands on the sandpaper and say 'Rough'. 3. Have them rub the silk and say 'Smooth', identifying contrasting textures.
activity_photo: [Image: Child rubbing their fingers on rough sandpaper]

activity: Listening to a Ticking Clock Hidden in a Room
description: 1. Take a loud, ticking analog clock or a ticking metronome app. 2. Hide it behind a curtain or under a pillow. 3. Ask the child to be completely silent and use their ears to hunt down the sound.
activity_photo: [Image: Child listening quietly to find a hidden clock]

description: 1. Cut squares of red, blue, and yellow transparent cellophane. 2. Hand one to the child. 3. Show them how to hold it up to their eyes to see the whole room turn a different color.
activity_photo: [Image: Child looking through a piece of blue plastic]

activity: Playing with Warm Soapy Water in a Basin
description: 1. Fill a low basin with safely warm water and mild dish soap to create huge bubbles. 2. Drop in a few plastic cups. 3. Let the child plunge their hands in, exploring the slippery water and airy foam.
activity_photo: [Image: Child playing happily in a tub of bubbles]

activity: Rubbing Lotion on Arms and Legs
description: 1. Squeeze a small dollop of baby lotion onto the child's hands. 2. Instruct them to rub it into their own arms and legs. 3. This provides deep proprioceptive pressure and reinforces body part identification.
activity_photo: [Image: Child rubbing lotion onto their own leg]

activity: Brushing Skin with a Soft Makeup Brush
description: 1. Take a large, clean, fluffy makeup brush. 2. Gently and slowly drag it down the infant's arms, legs, and back. 3. The incredibly soft, predictable stroke helps desensitize the skin and calms the nervous system.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent lightly brushing infant's arm with a soft brush]

activity: Finding a Toy Hidden Under a Cup
description: 1. Show the child a small toy car. 2. Place it on the floor and cover it with an opaque plastic cup while they watch. 3. Ask, 'Where is the car?' and let them lift the cup to find it, practicing object permanence.
activity_photo: [Image: Child lifting a cup to reveal a hidden toy car]

description: 1. Throw three pairs of vastly different, distinct socks into a pile. 2. Pick up one sock and hold it out. 3. Ask the child to dig through the pile and find the exact matching 'friend'.
activity_photo: [Image: Child holding up two identical striped socks]

activity: Pointing to the 'Big' Ball vs. 'Small' Ball
description: 1. Place a large beach ball and a small tennis ball on the floor. 2. Do not point. Simply ask, 'Can you touch the BIG ball?' 3. They must visually process size difference to make the correct choice.
toy_photo: [Image: Large and small balls side by side]
activity_photo: [Image: Child touching the large beach ball]

activity: Stacking Three Blocks to Reach a High Toy
description: 1. Tape a sticker or place a toy high up on a wall where the child cannot reach. 2. Give them three sturdy cardboard blocks. 3. Encourage them to figure out how to stack the blocks to create a step stool to reach the goal.
activity_photo: [Image: Child stacking blocks to step up and reach a toy]

activity: Sorting Red Blocks from Blue Blocks
description: 1. Dump a mix of red and blue blocks on the floor. 2. Set out a red piece of paper and a blue piece of paper. 3. Show the child how to put the red blocks on the red paper, and blue on blue.
tools: Red and blue blocks, colored paper
toy_photo: [Image: Red and blue blocks mixed up]
activity_photo: [Image: Child placing a blue block onto blue paper]

activity: Turning a Puzzle Piece to Fit the Hole
description: 1. Give the child a chunky wooden shape puzzle. 2. Hand them a triangle piece upside down. 3. They must problem-solve by physically turning and rotating the piece until the angles align with the hole.
activity_photo: [Image: Child rotating a puzzle piece to make it fit]

activity: Pointing to the Correct Animal Sound
description: 1. Place a toy dog, cat, and cow on the table. 2. Make a loud 'Moo!' sound. 3. Ask the child to point to the animal that makes that noise, linking auditory memory to a physical object.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pointing to a toy cow after hearing a moo]

activity: Retrieving a Toy with a Stick/Tool
description: 1. Roll a ball under the sofa, just out of arm's reach. 2. Lay a long cardboard wrapping paper tube nearby. 3. Wait for the child to realize they can use the tube as a tool to sweep the ball out.
activity_photo: [Image: Child using a cardboard tube to reach under a couch]

activity: Opening a Small Tupperware Box to Find a Snack
description: 1. Place a highly desired snack inside a clear plastic container with a simple snap-on lid. 2. Hand it to the child. 3. They can see the reward but must figure out how to pry the plastic lid off to get it.
toy_photo: [Image: Plastic food container with a snack inside]
activity_photo: [Image: Child struggling to pull the lid off a container]

activity: Placing Circles in a Circle Sorter
description: 1. Tape over all the holes of a shape sorter bucket except the circle hole. 2. Give the child only the round cylindrical blocks. 3. Have them practice the basic spatial concept of dropping the round peg into the round hole.
toy_photo: [Image: Shape sorter with only the round hole open]
activity_photo: [Image: Child pushing a round block through a hole]

activity: Passing a Ball Back and Forth
description: 1. Sit on the floor facing the child with your legs spread wide. 2. Roll a ball to them. 3. Say 'Your turn!' and encourage them to roll it back, establishing the fundamental rhythm of social reciprocity.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent and child rolling a ball back and forth]

description: 1. Make a crying sound and hold a teddy bear. 2. Say, 'Oh no, the bear is sad.' 3. Ask the child, 'Can you make him feel better?' and encourage them to hug or pat the bear to build empathy.
activity_photo: [Image: Child giving a tight hug to a teddy bear]

description: 1. When a family member or guest leaves the house, stand at the door with the infant. 2. Say 'Bye-bye!' cheerfully. 3. Take their hand and physically help them wave, modeling social parting rituals.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent helping infant wave out the front door]

activity: Looking in a Mirror and Pointing to 'Me'
description: 1. Sit in front of a mirror with the child. 2. Point to your reflection and say 'Mommy/Daddy'. 3. Point to their reflection and say 'Who is that? That's [Child's Name]!' fostering self-recognition.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pointing to their own reflection in a mirror]

description: 1. When another person finishes a task (like building a tower or finishing a meal), say 'Yay! Good job!' 2. Clap your hands loudly. 3. Encourage the child to clap along, sharing in another person's joy.
activity_photo: [Image: Child clapping enthusiastically for someone else]

activity: Taking Turns Pushing a Toy Car
description: 1. Have one desirable toy car. 2. Push it and say 'My turn.' 3. Hand it to the child and say 'Your turn.' Gently enforce waiting for 5 seconds before asking for the car back, teaching delayed gratification.
activity_photo: [Image: Child waiting their turn to roll a toy car]

activity: Identifying a 'Happy' Face in a Book
description: 1. Open a picture book that shows clear facial expressions. 2. Point to a smiling character. 3. Ask the child, 'Look, is he happy or sad? Show me a happy face!' and smile broadly at them.
activity_photo: [Image: Child mimicking a smile seen in a book]

description: 1. When hugging the child, gently pat their back. 2. Say, 'Nice, gentle pats.' 3. If they hit or slap, hold their hand, model a soft pat, and praise them for showing gentle physical affection.
activity_photo: [Image: Child softly patting a parent's shoulder]

description: 1. After completing a fun task, hold your hand up flat. 2. Say, 'High five!' enthusiastically. 3. Gently tap their hand if they don't respond, teaching them this common celebratory social interaction.
activity_photo: [Image: Child giving an adult a high five]

description: 1. Cover your eyes with your own hands. 2. Pop your hands away and say 'Peek-a-boo!' with a big smile. 3. The predictable surprise builds a sense of safety, anticipation, and social bonding.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent playing peek-a-boo with a laughing baby]

description: 1. Show the child a picture or toy of a cow. 2. Exaggerate the sound: 'The cow says Moooo!' 3. Pause and look expectantly at the child, encouraging them to attempt mimicking the vowel-heavy sound.
activity_photo: [Image: Child making a 'moo' face holding a toy cow]

activity: Pointing to Body Parts when Named (Nose, Ears)
description: 1. Sit facing the child. 2. Say, 'Where is your nose?' and wait. 3. If they don't point, tap their nose gently. Repeat with ears, eyes, and mouth to build receptive language vocabulary.
toy_photo: [Image: Face with arrows pointing to features]
activity_photo: [Image: Child poking their own nose happily]

description: 1. Knock a block off the table intentionally. 2. Throw your hands up and say 'Uh-oh!' clearly. 3. Repeat this routine whenever something falls, providing a consistent, easy-to-say exclamatory word model.
activity_photo: [Image: Infant looking at a dropped toy while parent says 'uh-oh']

activity: Following a One-Step Direction ('Bring the cup')
description: 1. Point to a cup sitting on the table across the room. 2. Say clearly, 'Bring me the cup, please.' 3. Wait for the child to process the auditory command, fetch the item, and return it to you.
activity_photo: [Image: Child walking toward parent holding a cup]

description: 1. Give the infant a single puff or bite of food. 2. Before giving the next bite, tap your fingertips together and say 'More'. 3. Encourage them to mimic the hand sign to bridge the gap before verbal speech.
activity_photo: [Image: Infant signing 'more' with their hands]

activity: Blowing Air out to make a 'P' sound
description: 1. Press your lips tightly together and forcefully blow air out to say 'Puh! Puh!'. 2. Hold a tissue in front of your mouth so it moves when you say it. 3. Have the child try to make the tissue move with their own 'Puh'.
activity_photo: [Image: Child blowing hard to make a 'P' sound]

description: 1. Lean in close to the child's ear. 2. Whisper a word very quietly, like 'Banana'. 3. Have them try to whisper a word back to you, practicing volume control and breath regulation for speech.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent whispering into child's ear]

activity: Choosing Between Two Options ('Apple or Banana?')
description: 1. Hold up an apple in one hand and a banana in the other. 2. Ask, 'Do you want the apple or the banana?' 3. Withhold the item until they attempt to verbalize or gesture toward the specific word they want.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pointing and vocalizing their choice of fruit]

description: 1. Ask the infant a question you know they will refuse (e.g., offering a toy they dislike). 2. Say 'No' while shaking your head exaggeratedly. 3. Praise them when they use the head shake to communicate refusal non-verbally.
activity_photo: [Image: Infant shaking head side to side to say no]

description: 1. Push a toy car across the floor. 2. Make a loud, continuous 'Vrooooom' sound. 3. Encourage the child to push their car and practice making prolonged vowel sounds to mimic the engine.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pushing a car making a 'vroom' face]

description: 1. Ensure the child is wearing loose-fitting socks. 2. Pull the heel of the sock down slightly for them. 3. Instruct them to grab the toe of the sock and pull hard to remove it completely by themselves.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pulling their own sock off by the toe]

activity: Wiping Face with a Damp Cloth
description: 1. After a messy meal, hand the child a damp, warm washcloth. 2. Tap your own chin and say, 'Wipe your face.' 3. Allow them to clumsily rub their mouth before you take the cloth to finish the job.
activity_photo: [Image: Child rubbing a wet cloth over their messy mouth]

activity: Helping to Push Arms through Sleeves
description: 1. Hold the child's jacket open behind them. 2. Guide their hand into the armhole. 3. Say, 'Push it through!' and encourage them to thrust their arm down the sleeve until their hand pops out.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pushing their arm deep into a coat sleeve]

activity: Drinking from an Open Cup with Assistance
description: 1. Pour one inch of water into a small, plastic, open cup. 2. Have the child hold it with two hands. 3. Keep your hands over theirs and gently help them tilt the cup to take a sip without spilling.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent guiding a child's hands to drink from an open cup]

activity: Using a Fork to Pierce Soft Melon
description: 1. Cut soft fruit like melon or banana into cubes. 2. Hand the child a toddler-safe fork. 3. Show them how to hold the handle and push down forcefully to stab the fruit before lifting it to their mouth.
activity_photo: [Image: Child using a fork to stab a piece of fruit]

activity: Throwing a Napkin in the Trash Can
description: 1. After a snack, hand the child a used paper napkin. 2. Point to the open trash can. 3. Say, 'Time to clean up. Put it in the trash.' and have them walk over to discard the item.
activity_photo: [Image: Child dropping a napkin into a trash bin]

description: 1. Put a smear of safe toothpaste on a toddler brush. 2. Let the child hold the brush and 'scrub' their own teeth first. 3. Praise their independence before taking the brush to finish cleaning thoroughly.
activity_photo: [Image: Child attempting to brush their own teeth]

description: 1. Ensure the child is wearing loose sweatpants. 2. At potty time or bath time, tell them to put their thumbs inside the waistband. 3. Instruct them to push the pants down past their hips to their knees.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pushing their pants down by the waistband]

activity: Placing Dirty Clothes in a Hamper
description: 1. After taking off their clothes for bath time, point to the laundry basket. 2. Say, 'Put your dirty shirt in the hamper.' 3. Encourage them to pick up the clothing and drop it in, building chore routines.
activity_photo: [Image: Child dropping a shirt into a laundry basket]

activity: Washing Hands with Soap at the Sink
description: 1. Stand the child on a stool at the sink. 2. Put a drop of soap on their wet hands. 3. Instruct them to rub their palms together to make bubbles, then hold their hands under the water to rinse.
activity_photo: [Image: Child rubbing soapy hands together under a faucet]

activity: Being Rolled tightly in a Blanket (Burrito)
description: 1. Lay a heavy blanket on the floor. 2. Have the child lay down on the edge. 3. Gently roll them up in the blanket, applying deep, calming pressure across their entire body.
activity_photo: [Image: Child smiling while rolled tightly in a blanket]

description: 1. Sit the child on top of a large, partially deflated yoga/exercise ball. 2. Hold them securely at the hips. 3. Bounce them gently up and down, requiring them to engage their core to stay upright.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent holding a child bouncing on a large ball]

activity: Hanging Upside Down over Parent's Lap
description: 1. Sit on a sofa. 2. Hold the child firmly by the thighs and let them lean backwards over your legs. 3. Let their head hang upside down momentarily to provide intense inner-ear vestibular input.
activity_photo: [Image: Child laughing while hanging upside down off parent's lap]

description: 1. Lay a strong blanket flat. 2. Place the infant in the middle. 3. Two adults pick up the ends of the blanket and sway it slowly back and forth like a hammock to soothe the nervous system.
activity_photo: [Image: Two adults gently swinging a baby in a blanket]

activity: Pushing against a Wall with Both Hands
description: 1. Have the child stand facing a solid wall. 2. Tell them to place their palms flat against it. 3. Instruct them to lean forward and 'push the wall over' as hard as they can to get heavy joint compression.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pushing hard against a wall]

activity: Carrying a Backpack filled with Two Books
description: 1. Place two heavy books in a toddler-sized backpack. 2. Strap the backpack securely onto the child. 3. Have them walk around the house; the weight provides organizing deep pressure to their shoulders.
activity_photo: [Image: Child walking while wearing a weighted backpack]

description: 1. Find a soft, safe grassy hill. 2. Have the child lie down horizontally at the top with their arms crossed. 3. Encourage them to roll like a log all the way to the bottom to experience rapid rotary motion.
activity_photo: [Image: Child rolling down a hill laughing]

activity: Being Spun Slowly in an Office Chair
description: 1. Sit the child deeply and securely into a swivel office chair. 2. Hold them safely. 3. Slowly spin the chair 3 times in one direction, pause for a few seconds, then spin 3 times in the other direction.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent spinning a toddler slowly in a desk chair]

activity: Doing a Forward Somersault with Help
description: 1. Use a soft carpet or gymnastics mat. 2. Have the child crouch and tuck their chin firmly to their chest. 3. Gently lift their hips and guide them over into a slow, safe forward roll.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent assisting a child through a forward roll]

description: 1. Take large, heavy cushions off the couch and lay them on the floor. 2. Lift one up slightly like a tunnel. 3. As the child crawls under, let the cushion rest heavily on their back, providing squishy resistance.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pushing their way under heavy cushions]

description: 1. Provide a stiff shoelace and a bowl of jumbo wooden beads. 2. The child must hold the bead steady in one hand. 3. They must visually align and push the tip of the lace through the hole with the other hand.
toy_photo: [Image: Jumbo wooden beads with a wide hole]
activity_photo: [Image: Child threading string through a large bead]

activity: Tracing a Thick Line with a Crayon
description: 1. Use a dark marker to draw a very thick, straight line across a piece of paper. 2. Give the child a crayon. 3. Instruct them to try and draw directly on top of your line, linking visual tracking to hand movement.
activity_photo: [Image: Child trying to trace a line with a crayon]

description: 1. Give the child 5 plastic drinking cups. 2. Show them how to turn one upside down and balance another on top. 3. Encourage them to carefully place all 5 cups in a vertical tower without knocking it over.
activity_photo: [Image: Child carefully balancing plastic cups into a tower]

description: 1. Sit on the floor facing the child with legs in a V. 2. Roll a medium-sized ball smoothly toward them. 3. The child must watch the approaching object and bring their hands together at the right moment to trap it.
activity_photo: [Image: Child trapping a rolling ball between their hands]

activity: Throwing a Beanbag into a Laundry Basket
description: 1. Place a wide laundry basket 3 feet away. 2. Hand the child several soft beanbags. 3. Instruct them to look at the basket, pull their arm back, and toss the bag forward into the target.
activity_photo: [Image: Child tossing a beanbag into a basket]

description: 1. Draw a massive circle taking up a whole piece of paper. 2. Give the child a marker. 3. Tell them to color the 'inside', requiring them to recognize the visual boundary line and attempt to stop their hand.
activity_photo: [Image: Child trying to color inside a drawn circle]

activity: Tapping a Balloon to Keep it in the Air
description: 1. Blow up a balloon and toss it in the air. 2. Tell the child, 'Don't let it touch the ground!' 3. They must constantly visually track the balloon and rapidly coordinate their hands to smack it upward.
activity_photo: [Image: Child looking up and batting a balloon into the air]

activity: Following a Flashlight Beam on the Wall
description: 1. Dim the lights and turn on a flashlight. 2. Move the beam of light slowly across the wall. 3. Ask the child to chase the light and 'tag' it with their hand, bridging visual input to gross motor action.
activity_photo: [Image: Child slapping a wall trying to catch a light beam]

description: 1. Provide a chunky plastic pegboard and several pegs. 2. The child must pick up the peg, visually locate an empty hole, and align their hand to push the peg directly downward into the space.
activity_photo: [Image: Child pushing a peg into a hole on a board]

activity: Connecting Two Dots with a Marker
description: 1. Draw a red dot and a blue dot 6 inches apart on a paper. 2. Give the child a crayon. 3. Ask them to draw a road from the red dot to the blue dot, requiring visual planning to hit a specific target.
activity_photo: [Image: Child drawing a line connecting two dots]

activity: Sucking Applesauce through a Thick Straw
description: 1. Put smooth applesauce in a cup. 2. Insert a wide, smoothie-style straw. 3. Instruct the child to suck the heavy puree up the straw, which demands intense lip seal and cheek muscle strength.
toy_photo: [Image: Cup with puree and a wide straw]
activity_photo: [Image: Child sucking hard on a thick straw]

description: 1. Dip a bubble wand into solution and hold it in front of the child's mouth. 2. Tell them to make an 'O' with their lips. 3. Have them blow a steady stream of air through the circle to create bubbles.
activity_photo: [Image: Child with puckered lips blowing through a bubble wand]

activity: Licking a Popsicle with an Extended Tongue
description: 1. Give the child a frozen fruit popsicle. 2. Remind them not to bite it. 3. Encourage them to stick their tongue out as far as it goes to lick the treat, building tongue extension and lateral movement.
activity_photo: [Image: Child sticking tongue out to lick a popsicle]

activity: Biting and Chewing a Crunchy Carrot Stick
description: 1. Hand the child a raw, peeled carrot stick. 2. Have them bite a piece off using their front teeth. 3. Encourage them to move the piece to their back molars to crunch it, building jaw stability and strength.
activity_photo: [Image: Child biting hard into a crunchy carrot stick]

description: 1. Look in the mirror with the child. 2. Press your lips together tight and puff your cheeks up like a blowfish. 3. Encourage the child to copy you and hold the air in for 3 seconds without letting it escape.
activity_photo: [Image: Child puffing cheeks full of air in a mirror]

description: 1. Tell the child to close their mouth completely. 2. Start humming a loud, simple tune like 'Row Your Boat'. 3. Have them try to hum along, which forces them to vibrate their vocal cords while maintaining lip closure.
activity_photo: [Image: Child humming with lips pressed tightly together]

description: 1. Demonstrate making a 'click-clack' sound by suctioning your tongue to the roof of your mouth and dropping it. 2. Tell the child it's a horse galloping. 3. Let them attempt to replicate the complex tongue elevation.
activity_photo: [Image: Child concentrating to make a clicking sound with their tongue]

description: 1. Sit facing the infant. 2. Exaggerate popping your lips open and closed to make loud smacking noises. 3. This visual and auditory model encourages them to experiment with bringing their own lips together.
activity_photo: [Image: Parent smacking lips while baby watches intently]

activity: Holding Water in Mouth without Swallowing
description: 1. During bath time, take a tiny sip of water. 2. Puff your cheeks slightly and point to the water in your mouth. 3. Challenge the child to take a sip and hold it for 3 seconds before spitting it out, building muscle control.
activity_photo: [Image: Child holding water in their cheeks]

description: 1. Hold a colorful plastic pinwheel in front of the child's face. 2. Instruct them to take a deep breath in through their nose. 3. Have them pucker their lips and blow out hard to make the toy spin rapidly.
activity_photo: [Image: Child blowing hard on a spinning pinwheel]
